The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(M,g)$ be a boundaryless Riemannian manifold. An open set $W\subseteq M$ is called **strongly geodesically convex** here when, for every ordered pair $(x,y)\in W\times W$, there is a unique affinely parametrized geodesic $\gamma_{x,y}:[0,1]\to M$ that globally minimizes length from $x$ to $y$, its image lies in $W$, and $(x,y,t)\mapsto\gamma_{x,y}(t)$ is smooth.

Every point of $M$ has a strongly geodesically convex neighbourhood. More precisely, the neighbourhood may be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood of the point, and it may be chosen so that every piecewise smooth curve attaining the global minimum between two of its points is a monotone reparametrization of the displayed connector. Every nonempty intersection of a positive finite family of strongly geodesically convex open sets is again strongly geodesically convex.

Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g:X\to Y$ be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy $H:X\times[0,1]\to Y$. Then $f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)$ for every integer $n$. Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in $k$.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$ and any abelian group $G$, there is a natural exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\alpha}H^n(U;G)\oplus H^n(V;G)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^n(U\cap V;G)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^{n+1}(X;G)\to\cdots.$$
Here $\alpha$ is the pair of restrictions and $\beta([u],[v])=[u|_{U\cap V}-v|_{U\cap V}]$. Naturality means continuous maps $f:X\to X'$ with $f(U)\subseteq U'$ and $f(V)\subseteq V'$ for the ordered covers, and coefficient homomorphisms. The connector is specified in the proof with this difference sign. Negative-degree groups are zero.

Let $X$ be any topological space and $G$ an abelian group. Its **singular cochains with coefficients in $G$** are
$$C^n(X;G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(C_n(X;\mathbb Z),G)\quad(n\ge0),\qquad C^n(X;G)=0\quad(n<0),$$
where the chains are those of [[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]]. Addition and negatives of homomorphisms are pointwise. The **coboundary** is
$$\delta^n:C^n(X;G)\to C^{n+1}(X;G),\qquad \delta^n\varphi=\varphi\circ\partial_{n+1}$$
for $n\ge0$, and is zero for $n<0$. Composition with the homomorphism [[def-singular-boundary-operator|$\partial_{n+1}$]] is additive, so this is a homomorphism. The sign convention is positive: there is no extra degree sign on this composite. On a singular $(n+1)$-simplex it says
$$\delta^n\varphi(\sigma)=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i\varphi(\sigma\circ\delta_i),$$
where $\delta_i$ denotes the affine face map, distinct from the superscripted coboundary. In particular $\delta^0\varphi$ on an oriented path is its endpoint value minus its initial value.

By [[def-singular-simplex-and-singular-chain-group-with-coefficients]], the integer chains are finite sums on the specified simplex set $S_n(X)$. Thus a cochain is equivalently an arbitrary function $S_n(X)\to G$: the extension sends $\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma$ to $\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\varphi(\sigma)$. The sum is finite and the formal coefficients are unique. The cochain need not have finite support.

For a commutative unital ring $R$ and an $R$-module $G$, there is a canonical identification
$$C^n(X;G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_n(X;R),G).$$
Indeed the given chain convention is $C_n(X;R)=C_n(X;\mathbb Z)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R$. A homomorphism $\varphi$ on integer chains defines an $R$-linear map by $c\otimes r\mapsto r\varphi(c)$; the defining additive and integer-balanced tensor relations are preserved. Conversely evaluate an $R$-linear map on $c\otimes1$. These operations are inverse since $c\otimes r=r(c\otimes1)$, and they intertwine the two coboundaries because the coefficient boundary is $\partial\otimes1$. The construction also covers the zero ring with its unital zero module.

The resulting graded group and coboundary are called the **singular cochain complex**. The square-zero identity follows by precomposition with $\partial^2=0$ in the chain complex and is spelled out in the next lemma. If $X$ is empty there are no singular simplices, so every cochain group is zero; if $G=0$ the same is true. The extension and tensor formulas are uniquely specified and require no AC.

For a space $X$ and an abelian group $G$, a degree-$n$ **singular cocycle** is a cochain in $Z^n(X;G)=\ker\delta^n$ and a degree-$n$ **singular coboundary** belongs to $B^n(X;G)=\operatorname{im}\delta^{n-1}$, for the positive coboundary convention of [[def-singular-cochain-complex-with-coefficients]]. The square-zero lemma [[lem-the-singular-coboundary-squares-to-zero]] implies $B^n\subseteq Z^n$: if $\varphi=\delta^{n-1}\psi$, then $\delta^n\varphi=0$.

The **singular cohomology group with coefficients in $G$** is
$$H^n(X;G)=Z^n(X;G)/B^n(X;G)\quad(n\ge0),\qquad H^n(X;G)=0\quad(n<0).$$
This is the abelian quotient with addition $[\varphi]+[\psi]=[\varphi+\psi]$: changing either representative by a coboundary changes the sum by a coboundary. Thus two cocycles represent the same class exactly when their difference is $\delta^{n-1}\eta$ for some degree-$(n-1)$ cochain $\eta$. In degree zero, $B^0=0$ because $C^{-1}=0$; hence $H^0=\ker\delta^0$. The zero convention in negative degrees agrees with the same kernel/image construction on the zero cochain groups.

If coefficients are a module over a commutative ring, the same groups and maps are modules and linear maps, and this is their module quotient. Empty $X$ or zero coefficients give zero cohomology in every degree. The notation does not define cohomology as the dual of homology; such identifications require their own theorems. No choice of cocycle representatives and no AC is part of this definition.

Let $X$ be a topological space and let $n\geq 1$. For a singular $n$-simplex
$\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, its **singular boundary** is
$$\partial_n\sigma:=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\sigma\circ\delta_i\in C_{n-1}(X;\mathbb Z),$$
where the $\delta_i$ are the affine face maps from
[[def-singular-simplex-and-singular-chain-group-with-coefficients]].

Extend this formula $\mathbb Z$-linearly to a homomorphism
$$\partial_n:C_n(X;\mathbb Z)\to C_{n-1}(X;\mathbb Z).$$
For coefficients in an abelian group $G$, the boundary on $C_n(X;G)$ is the
tensor extension
$$\partial_n\otimes\operatorname{id}_G:C_n(X;G)\to C_{n-1}(X;G),$$
again denoted $\partial_n$.

The degree-zero boundary is the zero map
$$\partial_0:C_0(X;G)\to 0,$$
and for negative indices the chain groups are taken to be zero.

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and equip it with a Riemannian metric. An open set is strongly geodesically convex if every ordered pair of its points is joined by a unique affinely parametrized globally length-minimizing geodesic whose image stays in the set and whose connector depends smoothly on the endpoints. There are finitely many such open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ covering $F$, every nonempty finite intersection of which is strongly geodesically convex. Let $K$ be the finite simplicial complex whose nonempty faces are the index sets $\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for which $U_\sigma=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i$ is nonempty. Then its usual geometric realization $|K|$ is homotopy equivalent to $F$. For $F=\varnothing$, take $N=0$ and $K=\varnothing$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the convex neighborhoods cover \(F\); compactness gives a finite subcover \(U_1,\ldots,U_N\), with \(N\geq1\) when \(F\ne\varnothing\). Every nonempty finite intersection \(U_{i_1}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_s}\) is strongly geodesically convex. Choosing a point in that intersection, the unique minimizing geodesics to it give a continuous contraction to the point; by [F2] and the singular cochain definition in [F3], its cohomology is \(k\) in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. For a point, this follows from the unique singular \(n\)-simplex: its boundary coefficient is \(1\) for even \(n\) and \(0\) for odd \(n\), so the positive-degree cochain complex is alternately identity and zero and has zero cohomology. The nerve has at most \(N\) vertices, hence is finite, and [F4] gives a homotopy equivalence between its realization and \(F\). [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, construct]

We prove by induction on the number \(m\geq1\) of members of a finite good cover that its union has cohomology zero in every degree \(q\geq m\). For \(m=1\), step 1.1 makes the member contractible, giving the claim. For \(m>1\), write \(A=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_{m-1}\) and \(B=U_m\). The intersection \(A\cap B\) is covered by the \(m-1\) sets \(U_i\cap U_m\), whose nonempty finite intersections are contractible by step 1.1. The induction hypothesis gives \(H^q(A;k)=0\) and \(H^{q-1}(A\cap B;k)=0\) for \(q\geq m\); also \(H^q(B;k)=0\) since \(q>0\). The exact segment \(H^{q-1}(A\cap B;k)\to H^q(A\cup B;k)\to H^q(A;k)\oplus H^q(B;k)\) from [F3] therefore forces \(H^q(A\cup B;k)=0\). [F3, step 1.1, induction, algebra]

Apply step 2.1 to the selected finite cover of \(F\) to get \(H^q(F;k)=0\) for \(q\geq N\). Every homogeneous factor of a product of \(N\) elements of \(J\) has positive degree, so the product has degree at least \(N\) and vanishes; expanding finite sums proves \(J^N=0\). For empty \(F\), every cohomology group is zero by the empty-space cochain complex, so \(N=1\) works. [F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

boundaries.evidence: step 3.1 treats empty F by its zero cochain complex; the Statement sets K empty, N=1 and J=0.
step 3.1 gives J=0 for empty F; for zero-dimensional compact F a finite singleton cover has no positive cohomology, so the same positive-ideal conclusion holds.
step 2.1 has the one-member-cover induction base: its union is contractible and H^q vanishes for q>=1; the Statement permits N=1.
step 1.1 permits empty intersections by imposing contractibility only on nonempty ones; step 2.1 therefore also covers disconnected finite covers.

boundaries.reason: Cohomological vanishing above N and nilpotence are discrete grading assertions, with no interval endpoint or manifold-boundary claim.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 chooses a contraction point only inside a nonempty finite intersection. A1 supplies the convex-cover prerequisites; compactness selects finitely many cover members.

boundaries.reason: The Statement derives nilpotence from degree vanishing; it does not assert a biconditional between finite CW type and a nilpotent positive ideal.
No converse from J^N=0 to vanishing in all degrees q>=N is claimed; step 3.1 uses the already established vanishing to kill products.

Assume AC and let $n\geq1$. Let $E\mathbb U(n)$ be the model $V_n(\mathbb C^\infty)$ of the
universal principal $\mathbb U(n)$-bundle, so that
$B\mathbb U(n)=E\mathbb U(n)/\mathbb U(n)=\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb C^\infty)$,
and let $T^n\subseteq\mathbb U(n)$ be the maximal torus of diagonal unitary
matrices. Then the complete flag bundle of the universal rank-$n$ complex
bundle is homotopy equivalent over $B\mathbb U(n)$ to $BT^n$, and $BT^n$ is
homotopy equivalent to $(\mathbb{CP}^\infty)^n$.

Here one may take the product of the standard circle classifying bundles as
the model of $BT^n$; its map to $B\mathbb U(n)$ is the sum of the coordinate
lines. The flag identification uses the equivalent quotient model
$V_n(\mathbb C^\infty)/T^n$, with its displayed map to $B\mathbb U(n)$.

Under the explicit equivalence constructed below the Chern roots $t_i=c_1(L_i)$ of
[[def-complex-flag-bundle-and-chern-roots]] are the coordinate generators:
$$H^*(BT^n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[t_1,\dots,t_n],$$
the $i$-th tautological line being the pullback of the universal line from the

$\mathbb Z[t_1,\dots,t_n]$.

derivations.claim: If \(r=0\), \(BT\) is a point and the CW and paracompact assertions reduce to the compact manifold \(F\). For \(r\geq1\), [F1] gives \(BT\) its ordinary product CW topology, and [F3] makes it paracompact Hausdorff. By [F2], choose a finite CW complex \(K\) and a homotopy equivalence \(h:F\to K\). Since \(K\) is finite, its CW product with the CW complex \(BT\) has the ordinary product topology; hence \(BT\times K\) is a CW complex. The maps \(\mathrm{id}_{BT}\times h\) and the product of a homotopy inverse with \(\mathrm{id}_{BT}\) are homotopy inverses, since their coordinate homotopies are continuous in the product topology. Thus \(BT\times F\) has CW type. If \(F=\varnothing\), take \(K=\varnothing\). [A1, F1, F2, F3, construct]

If \(F=\varnothing\), the product is empty and paracompact Hausdorff, so assume \(F\ne\varnothing\). To prove paracompactness of \(BT\times F\), let \(\mathcal U\) be an open cover. For each \(x\in BT\) and \(y\in F\), choose a product neighborhood \(O_{x,y}\times V_{x,y}\) of \((x,y)\) contained in some member \(U_{x,y}\in\mathcal U\). Compactness of \(F\) selects finitely many \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) whose \(V_{x,y_j}\) cover \(F\). Then \(O_x=\bigcap_{j=1}^m O_{x,y_j}\) is an open neighborhood of \(x\), and \(O_x\times F\) is covered by \(U_{x,y_1},\ldots,U_{x,y_m}\). Paracompactness of \(BT\) gives a locally finite open refinement \(\{W_\alpha\}\) of \(\{O_x\}\). For each \(\alpha\), choose \(x_\alpha\) with \(W_\alpha\subseteq O_{x_\alpha}\); the finitely many sets \((W_\alpha\times F)\cap U_{x_\alpha,y_j}\) cover \(W_\alpha\times F\), are open, and refine \(\mathcal U\). They are locally finite because a neighborhood \(N\times F\) meets sets indexed by only those \(\alpha\) for which \(W_\alpha\) meets \(N\), a finite set. Hence \(BT\times F\) is paracompact. It is Hausdorff as a product of Hausdorff spaces. The point and rank-zero cases satisfy the same conclusions. [F1, F3, given, construct] ∎

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by

Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ be a compact torus with its standard product Lie-group smooth structure and period-one basis, and let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, not assumed compact, with a smooth left action $a:T\times M\to M$. Work over $\mathbb R$ and use the chosen product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ and $BT=ET/T$ from the preceding coefficient lemma. Give $ET\times M$ the right diagonal action $(e,p)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot p)$ and define
$$ET\times_T M:=(ET\times M)/T.$$
The **Borel equivariant cohomology** is the graded ring
$$H_T^*(M;\mathbb R):=H_{\mathrm{sing}}^*(ET\times_T M;\mathbb R).$$
For $M=\{\ast\}$ this gives $H_T^*(\ast;\mathbb R)=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$; the selected degree-two normalization in $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ is the isomorphism established in the preceding coefficient lemma.

The quotient map $q:ET\times M\to ET\times_T M$ and projection
$\pi([e,p])=[e]$ give the associated-space square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}ET\times M&\xrightarrow{q}&ET\times_T M\\\downarrow\operatorname{pr}_1&&\downarrow\pi\\ET&\xrightarrow{q_T}&BT\end{array}$$
Its TikZ source is
```latex
\begin{tikzcd}
ET\times M \arrow[r,"q"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_1"'] & ET\times_T M \arrow[d,"\pi"]\\
ET \arrow[r,"q_T"'] & BT
\end{tikzcd}
```
where $q_T:ET\to BT$ is the orbit quotient. The projection $\pi$ is
well-defined because $[e\cdot t]=[e]$ for every $t\in T$. The square
commutes because both composites send $(e,p)$ to $[e]$.

Let $\mathfrak t=T_eT$, with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ and dual basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. Regard $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ as a polynomial algebra by assigning each linear generator degree two. Use the trivial $T$-action on this polynomial factor, and the induced left action $t\cdot\alpha=(a_{t^{-1}})^*\alpha$ on forms. It is a left action because pullback reverses composition: $a_{t^{-1}}^*a_{s^{-1}}^*=(a_{s^{-1}}\circ a_{t^{-1}})^*=a_{(ts)^{-1}}^*$. The **Cartan complex** is the graded-commutative algebra
$$C_T(M):=\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\Omega^*(M)\bigr)^T,$$
with multiplication $(P\otimes\alpha)(Q\otimes\beta)=PQ\otimes(\alpha\wedge\beta)$, where $\wedge$ is the differential-form wedge product and all tensor products are algebraic. The superscript denotes the fixed subspace for the diagonal action, and a polynomial of degree $j$ tensored with a $k$-form has total degree $2j+k$. For $\xi\in\mathfrak t$, use the library fundamental vector field
$$X_\xi(p)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}\exp_T(-s\xi)\cdot p.$$
On polynomial-valued forms define the degree-one Cartan operator
$$d_T(P\otimes\alpha)=P\otimes d\alpha-\sum_{i=1}^r(u_iP)\otimes\iota_{X_{e_i}}\alpha,$$
extended linearly. The tensor $\sum_i u_i\otimes X_{e_i}$ is basis-independent. The **Cartan equivariant cohomology** in this item means $H^*(C_T(M),d_T)$; the proof below establishes $d_T^2=0$ on $C_T(M)$.

This definition does not assert a general isomorphism between the Borel and Cartan cohomology rings. It defines neither equivariant Chow groups nor equivariant quotient-stack Borel–Moore homology, and no rational-coefficient comparison is being used in the real Cartan complex.

period-one tangent basis. Identify $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with the
multiplicative unit circle by $\epsilon([t])=e^{2\pi i t}$ and transfer its
right action to Milnor's countable-join model $E_{S^1}$; put

factor and $e_i^*$ its dual. Let $u=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})$ be the integral
degree-two generator of $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty};\mathbb Z)$ defined by the

complex line, and let $u_{\mathbb R}$ be its image under change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$. Under the product quotient identification
$BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$, write $u_i$ for the pullback of
$u_{\mathbb R}$ from the $i$th factor. Then
$$H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2,$$
and the chosen identification $e_i^*\mapsto u_i$ is a graded-algebra
isomorphism from $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$, with its
linear generators assigned degree two. For $r=0$, both rings are $\mathbb R$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume countable choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with its product Lie-group structure, and let $M$ be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let $a:T\times M\to M$ be a jointly smooth left action. Then $M$ admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under $a$. Its fixed set
$$
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
$$
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for each $p\in F$. The orthogonal normal bundle $\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F$ has no nonzero $T$-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of $F$, its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of $T$, with constant multiplicities; equivalently, $\nu_F$ admits a smooth $T$-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ and use the product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$, $BT=ET/T$, with right diagonal action $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, put $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})$ is the degree-two class of the $i$th coordinate character line. For a smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$, set $L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi$, with the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. If $\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}$ for $\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r$, then $c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i$. Define $\mathscr S_T(k)$ to consist of $1$ and all finite products of $c_1(L_\chi)$ for nontrivial characters $\chi$. This is a multiplicative subset of $A_T(k)$ with $0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)$. For a topological space $X$ with a continuous left $T$-action, set $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$, with its $A_T(k)$-module structure induced by $ET\times_T X\to BT$. For an $A_T(k)$-module $N$, its localization $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N$ consists of fractions $n/s$, with $n\in N$, $s\in\mathscr S_T(k)$, and $n/s=n'/s'$ exactly when $u(s'n-sn')=0$ for some $u\in\mathscr S_T(k)$; addition is $(n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')$, and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)$. For $r=0$, there are no nontrivial characters and $\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}$.

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let $k$ be a field. There is a finite CW complex $K$ homotopy equivalent to $F$, and an integer $N\geq1$ such that $H^q(F;k)=0$ for every $q\geq N$. Consequently the ideal $J=\bigoplus_{q>0}H^q(F;k)$ in the graded cohomology ring satisfies $J^N=0$. If $F=\varnothing$, take $K=\varnothing$, $N=1$, and $J=0$.

Assume AC. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then $BT\times F$ is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex $K$ such that $BT\times F\simeq BT\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, and use $E_T=(E_{S^1})^r$, the product of the right Milnor join models, with $BT=E_T/T$. For the $i$th coordinate character $\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)$, let $L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}$ be the associated complex line bundle over $BT$, with the right diagonal equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)$. Then
$$
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
$$
Every smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$ is uniquely $\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)$ for $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r$, and its associated line satisfies $c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i$. In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, $H_q(BT;k)$ is finite-dimensional in every degree $q$. For $r=0$, $BT$ is a point and its rational cohomology is $\mathbb Q$.

Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring. Give the graded tensor product the multiplication
$$(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=(-1)^{|b||a'|}(a\smile a')\otimes(b\smile b').$$
For arbitrary spaces $X,Y$, external product $a\times b=\operatorname{pr}_X^*a\smile\operatorname{pr}_Y^*b$ gives a unital graded-ring homomorphism to $H^*(X\times Y;R)$. This multiplicativity requires no AC.

Assume in addition AC, that $R$ is a PID, and that either every $H_q(Y;R)$ or every $H_p(X;R)$ is finite free over $R$. Then this homomorphism is an isomorphism.

For CW pairs $(X,A),(Y,B)$ with supplied characteristic maps, relative external product is likewise a graded-ring homomorphism
$$H^*(X,A;R)\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}_R H^*(Y,B;R)\longrightarrow H^*(X\times Y,(A\times Y)\cup(X\times B);R),$$
where the hat denotes the displayed graded multiplication on the ordinary graded direct-sum tensor product, not a completion. Relative rings need not have units. This relative multiplicativity is choice-free for every commutative unital $R$. Under AC and the PID hypothesis it is an isomorphism if either every $H_q(Y,B;R)$ or every $H_p(X,A;R)$ is finite free. Neither additive assertion requires bounded dimension or finite-rank singular chain groups. Products have their ordinary product topologies; AC enters only in additive bijectivity.

For a well-pointed topological group $G$ of CW type, the diagonal action on Milnor's $EG$ is free, $EG$ is contractible, and

$$ p:EG\longrightarrow BG $$

is a numerable principal $G$-bundle. The numeration satisfies the library's support-subordinate convention, not merely cozero containment.

The embeddings

$$e\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i,\qquad o\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i+1$$

are $G$-equivariantly homotopic to the identity. If $a,b:T\to EG$ are
continuous equivariant maps, then
$(1-t)e(a(-))+t\,o(b(-))$ is a continuous equivariant homotopy.

For $G=S^1$ or $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the selected compact-group topology identifies $BG$ with the standard weak CW colimit of the finite projective quotients $\mathbb{CP}^N$ or $\mathbb{RP}^N$, respectively.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Every open cover
of a paracompact Hausdorff space admits a locally finite partition of unity
subordinate to it.

Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal U$ be an open cover of $X$. A
family $\{\varphi_s:X\to[0,1]\}_{s\in S}$ is a **partition of unity** when each
$\varphi_s$ is continuous, the family of cozero sets
$\{\operatorname{coz}(\varphi_s)\}_{s\in S}$ is locally finite, and
$$\sum_{s\in S}\varphi_s(x)=1\quad\text{for every }x\in X.$$
The sum is unambiguous because local finiteness says that only finitely many
summands are nonzero near, and hence at, any fixed point.

It is **subordinate to $\mathcal U$** when for every $s\in S$ some
$U\in\mathcal U$ contains the support
$$\operatorname{supp}(\varphi_s):=\overline{\operatorname{coz}(\varphi_s)}.$$
Here cozero sets and zero sets have the meanings of
[[def-zero-sets-and-cozero-sets]].

Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\xi\to B$ be a metric rank-$n$ real
vector bundle.  Its **$R$-orientation local system** $\mathcal O_R(\xi)$ has
stalk
$$\mathcal O_R(\xi)_b=H^n(D(\xi_b),S(\xi_b);R).$$
On each bundle chart the fiber disk pairs identify with the standard disk
pair.  On overlaps, the linear transition functions induce units on its top
relative cohomology; these units are locally constant and satisfy the cocycle
law.  They therefore define a rank-one local system, whose path transport is
the corresponding composite of overlap units.  Metric changes give the same
system through the canonical radial pair isomorphisms.

The preceding disk-pair calculation identifies every stalk with a free
rank-one $R$-module.  An **$R$-orientation** is a section
$o=(o_b)$ of $\mathcal O_R(\xi)$ such that every $o_b$ generates its stalk;
equivalently it is a compatible locally constant family of fiber generators.
The bundle is **$R$-oriented** when such a section is supplied.

For $R=\mathbb F_2$, each one-dimensional stalk has exactly one nonzero
generator and every transition automorphism fixes it, so every real vector
bundle is canonically mod-two oriented.  Over $\mathbb Z$, a loop whose
monodromy sends a generator to its negative prevents an integral orientation:
compatibility would require $1=-1$ in $\mathbb Z$.

For rank zero the stalk is $H^0(*,\varnothing;R)=R$ and the unit gives the
standard orientation.  Empty bases have the unique empty section.  The zero
ring has its unique (zero) cyclic generator.  Identity and constant paths act
identically, reversed paths give inverse units, and no family of generators is
selected in making the definition.  It is choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly as in the general Thom theorem, and let
$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

Assume AC and work over bases in the scope of the general Thom theorem. Let
$E\to B$ and $F\to B$ be $R$-oriented numerable real bundles of ranks $m,n\geq0$
with normalized Thom classes $u_E,u_F$ and Euler classes
$e(E),e(F)$. The coefficient ring $R$ is commutative and unital.
Every rank-zero input carries the standard unit orientation; the orientation
reversal assertion below applies only in positive rank. Both bases in a
pullback square are required to lie in the general Thom scope.

1. **Naturality.** For an orientation-preserving pullback square

   $$
   \begin{CD} f^*E @>>> E\\ @VVV @VVV\\ B' @>f>> B\end{CD}
   $$
   one has $e(f^*E)=f^*e(E)$.
2. **Orientation sign.** Over $R=\mathbb Z$ and $m>0$, reversing the orientation of $E$
   negates the class: $e(E,-o)=-e(E,o)$.
3. **Whitney product.** Give $E\oplus F$ the ordered direct-sum orientation.
   Then $e(E\oplus F)=e(E)e(F)$, including the rank-zero unit $e(0_B)=1$.
4. **Koszul sign.** The swap $E\oplus F\to F\oplus E$ changes the ordered-sum
   orientation by $(-1)^{mn}$. Consequently the Euler products in the two
   standard orders satisfy
   $$e(E)e(F)=(-1)^{mn}e(F)e(E).$$

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle with $n\geq1$
over a path-connected CW complex $B$ (or over one of the CW-type bases of
[[thm-integral-complex-projective-bundle-theorem]]). By that theorem there are
unique classes $a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)$, $1\leq i\leq n$, such that
$$x_E^{\,n}-a_1x_E^{\,n-1}+a_2x_E^{\,n-2}-\cdots+(-1)^na_n=0\qquad\text{in }H^{2n}(P(E);\mathbb Z),$$
where $x_E\in H^2(P(E);\mathbb Z)$ is the Euler class of the underlying real
bundle of the tautological line
([[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]]). The
**Chern classes** of $E$ are these coefficients:
$$c_i(E):=a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)\qquad(1\leq i\leq n),$$
completed by the conventions $c_0(E):=1\in H^0(B;\mathbb Z)$ and
$c_i(E):=0$ for $i>n$, and the **total Chern class** is the finite sum
$c(E):=\sum_{i\geq0}c_i(E)=1+c_1(E)+\cdots+c_n(E)\in H^*(B;\mathbb Z)$.

For the zero bundle of rank $0$ the conventions give $c(0_B)=1$. The definition
depends only on the isomorphism class of $E$, because an isomorphism of
bundles induces an isomorphism of projective bundles pulling $x$ back to $x$
and hence preserves the unique relation. For a complex line bundle $L\to B$ one
has $P(L)\cong B$ over $B$ with $\gamma_L$ corresponding to $L$ under that
identification, so the relation is $x_L-c_1(L)=0$; since $x_L=e(L_{\mathbb R})$
under the identification, this gives
$$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R}).$$
This is the normalization used throughout the page: the first Chern class of a
complex line is the Euler class of its underlying real bundle in the complex
orientation, not a separately chosen normalization.

derivations.claim: Fix a component \(F_0\). The action on \(F_0\) is trivial, so its Borel base is \(BT\times F_0\). By [F5], the Borel normal bundle is numerable and oriented; hence its Thom and Euler classes exist. By [F4], identify \(H_T^*(F_0;k)\) as the graded ring \(A_T(k)\otimes_kH^*(F_0;k)\). [A1, F1, F2, F4, F5]

Fix \(p\in F_0\). Restriction of \(e_T(\nu_F)\) along \(BT\times\{p\}\hookrightarrow BT\times F_0\) is the Euler class of the associated normal representation bundle over \(BT\). By [F1], that representation is a sum of nontrivial complex character lines. The associated bundle is the direct sum of the corresponding \(L_\chi\), with the stated multiplicities. Whitney multiplication in [F6] and \(e(L_\chi)=c_1(L_\chi)\) give the claimed product. Every factor is a generator of \(\mathscr S_T(k)\). [F1, F2, F5, F6, step 1.1]

Under the Künneth decomposition of step 1.1 write \(e_T(\nu_F)=e_0+n\), where \(e_0\in A_T(k)\otimes H^0(F_0;k)\) is the component detected by restriction to \(p\), and \(n\in A_T(k)\otimes H^{>0}(F_0;k)\). Step 2.1 shows \(e_0\) is a product of generators of \(\mathscr S_T(k)\), so it is invertible after localization. By [F3], the ideal \(J=A_T(k)\otimes H^{>0}(F_0;k)\) satisfies \(J^N=0\); therefore \(z=e_0^{-1}n\) is nilpotent, and
\[
e_T(\nu_F)^{-1}=e_0^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-z)^j
\]
is a finite inverse. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

There are finitely many components by [F1], so \(H_T^*(F;k)\) and its localization split into the finite product of the component rings treated in step 3.1. A finite tuple of units is a unit componentwise. If \(F=\varnothing\), its cohomology is the zero ring and its unique element is a unit; if a normal component has rank zero, its product in step 2.1 is \(1\). These cases include \(r=0\), trivial actions, and empty \(M\). [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

step 4.1 gives Euler class 1 for a rank-zero normal component and includes r=0 and trivial actions.
step 2.1 gives one character class for a single normal character line; that class lies in S and hence is invertible.
step 3.1 works with n=0 in the decomposition e=e_0+n, giving inverse e_0^-1; step 4.1 separately includes zero-rank normal components.

Assume AC and let $n\geq1$. Let $E\mathbb U(n)$ be the model $V_n(\mathbb C^\infty)$ of the
universal principal $\mathbb U(n)$-bundle, so that
$B\mathbb U(n)=E\mathbb U(n)/\mathbb U(n)=\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb C^\infty)$,
and let $T^n\subseteq\mathbb U(n)$ be the maximal torus of diagonal unitary
matrices. Then the complete flag bundle of the universal rank-$n$ complex
bundle is homotopy equivalent over $B\mathbb U(n)$ to $BT^n$, and $BT^n$ is
homotopy equivalent to $(\mathbb{CP}^\infty)^n$.

Here one may take the product of the standard circle classifying bundles as
the model of $BT^n$; its map to $B\mathbb U(n)$ is the sum of the coordinate
lines. The flag identification uses the equivalent quotient model
$V_n(\mathbb C^\infty)/T^n$, with its displayed map to $B\mathbb U(n)$.

Under the explicit equivalence constructed below the Chern roots $t_i=c_1(L_i)$ of
[[def-complex-flag-bundle-and-chern-roots]] are the coordinate generators:
$$H^*(BT^n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[t_1,\dots,t_n],$$
the $i$-th tautological line being the pullback of the universal line from the
$i$-th factor. The symmetric group $\Sigma_n$ acts by bundle maps over
$B\mathbb U(n)$, permuting the factors and the $t_i$, so the image of the flag
pullback $q^*$ is contained in the symmetric invariants of
$\mathbb Z[t_1,\dots,t_n]$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If $H$ is a closed subgroup of a
finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, then the left-coset space $G/H$, with
its quotient topology, has a unique smooth manifold structure for which

$$q:G\longrightarrow G/H,\qquad q(g)=gH,$$

is a surjective submersion and the left $G$-action is smooth. Moreover,
$\dim(G/H)=\dim G-\dim H$.

Assume AC. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then $BT\times F$ is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex $K$ such that $BT\times F\simeq BT\times K$.

Assume AC. Let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and equip it with a Riemannian metric. An open set is strongly geodesically convex if every ordered pair of its points is joined by a unique affinely parametrized globally length-minimizing geodesic whose image stays in the set and whose connector depends smoothly on the endpoints. There are finitely many such open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ covering $F$, every nonempty finite intersection of which is strongly geodesically convex. Let $K$ be the finite simplicial complex whose nonempty faces are the index sets $\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for which $U_\sigma=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i$ is nonempty. Then its usual geometric realization $|K|$ is homotopy equivalent to $F$. For $F=\varnothing$, take $N=0$ and $K=\varnothing$.

Assume AC. Let $p:S\to B$ be a numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with
compact Hausdorff fiber $F$ over a paracompact Hausdorff base $B$. Then $S$ is
paracompact and Hausdorff. If in addition $B$ is compactly generated, then
$S$ is compactly generated (and hence CGWH). If $B$ and $F$ have the homotopy
type of CW complexes, then $S$ has the homotopy type of a CW complex.

Consequently the total spaces of the projective bundle and of the flag bundle
of a numerable bundle with compact fiber over a paracompact Hausdorff CGWH base
of CW type are again paracompact Hausdorff CGWH spaces of CW type, and the same
holds for finitely many fiber products of such total spaces over $B$.

A **locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $F$** is a continuous map $p:E\to B$, an open cover $(U_i)_{i\in S}$ of $B$, and homeomorphisms
$$\theta_i:p^{-1}(U_i)\longrightarrow U_i\times F,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1\theta_i=p|_{p^{-1}(U_i)}.$$
Here bundle charts, including those used later for principal and associated bundles, are charts in ordinary topological spaces with ordinary product and subspace topologies. A bundle whose spaces are CGWH in addition can be considered in the CGWH fibration convention; we do not silently replace an ordinary product chart by a weaker k-product-chart assumption. Products and homeomorphisms have the meanings of [[thm-product-universal-property]] and [[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]].

On $U_i\cap U_j$, the coordinate change has the form $(b,x)\mapsto(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$, with continuous inverse $(b,y)\mapsto(b,g_{ij}(b,y))$. In particular each $g_{ji}(b,-)$ is a homeomorphism of $F$. The identities $g_{ii}(b,x)=x$ and $g_{ki}(b,x)=g_{kj}(b,g_{ji}(b,x))$ hold because the corresponding chart composites cancel. No topology on a homeomorphism group of $F$ is assumed.

The bundle is **numerable** when the data include a partition $(\rho_i:B\to[0,1])_{i\in S}$ with locally finite cozero sets, sum one, and
$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)=\overline{\{b:\rho_i(b)>0\}}\subseteq U_i.$$
This is the support-subordinate convention of [[def-partition-of-unity-subordinate-to-a-cover]]. Repeating a chart with multiple indices is allowed, so a partition subordinate to a refinement can be accompanied by an explicitly assigned original chart. Merely having pointwise finite sums or cozero containment is not this specified numerating data.

An empty base forces $E$ empty and allows the empty cover and partition. The fiber $F$ may be empty: then every chart domain, hence $E$, is empty even when $B$ is nonempty. When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.

Let $G$ be a topological group, as in [[def-topological-group]], with identity $1$. A **right principal $G$-bundle** is a continuous map $\pi:P\to B$ with a continuous right action $(p,g)\mapsto pg$, satisfying $p1=p$, $(pg)h=p(gh)$ and $\pi(pg)=\pi(p)$, together with equivariant bundle charts $\theta_i:\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times G$ over an open cover. Equivariance means $\theta_i(pg)=(b,ag)$ whenever $\theta_i(p)=(b,a)$. Charts use ordinary products as in [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]]. In each fiber the action is free and transitive: right multiplication on $G$ has those properties and the chart identifies the actions. Freeness alone is not the definition.

A **left $G$-space** is a topological space $F$ with a continuous map $(g,x)\mapsto gx$ such that $1x=x$ and $g(hx)=(gh)x$. Effectiveness of this action is not required. Define
$$P\times_G F=(P\times F)/\bigl((pg,x)\sim(p,gx)\bigr)$$
with the ordinary quotient topology, and write $[p,x]$ for its points. Precisely, the relation is the orbit relation of the right action $(p,x)\cdot g=(pg,g^{-1}x)$. Its action law is $((p,x)\cdot g)\cdot h=(pgh,h^{-1}g^{-1}x)=(p,x)\cdot(gh)$, and its generating relations are exactly the displayed ones. Thus the equivalence relation and quotient are defined without choosing orbit representatives.

The projection $r([p,x])=\pi(p)$ is well-defined and continuous by [[thm-quotient-universal-property]], since $(p,x)\mapsto\pi(p)$ is continuous and constant on every orbit. This is the **associated fiber-bundle construction**; the next proposition proves its local triviality and pullback property. The quotient construction and projection already make sense before that proof.

If $B$ is empty then $P$ is empty. If $F$ is empty the associated space is empty even for nonempty $B$; this is allowed by our bundle convention. For singleton $F$ the construction is the orbit projection of the principal bundle. For the trivial group it is the product with $F$ over the chart-identified base. No AC is used.

For every subspace $A\subseteq X$ and abelian group $G$ there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{j}H^n(X;G)\xrightarrow{r}H^n(A;G)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^{n+1}(X,A;G)\to\cdots.$$
Here $j$ comes from including the relative cochains, $r$ is restriction, and the connector sends a cocycle class $[a]$ to $[\delta\widetilde a]$, for any cochain extension $\widetilde a$ of $a$ to $X$. Negative groups are zero, so the sequence begins $0\to H^0(X,A;G)\to H^0(X;G)\to H^0(A;G)$.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$ and any abelian group $G$, there is a natural exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\alpha}H^n(U;G)\oplus H^n(V;G)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^n(U\cap V;G)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^{n+1}(X;G)\to\cdots.$$
Here $\alpha$ is the pair of restrictions and $\beta([u],[v])=[u|_{U\cap V}-v|_{U\cap V}]$. Naturality means continuous maps $f:X\to X'$ with $f(U)\subseteq U'$ and $f(V)\subseteq V'$ for the ordered covers, and coefficient homomorphisms. The connector is specified in the proof with this difference sign. Negative-degree groups are zero.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $S\subseteq R$ contain $1$, be closed under multiplication, and not contain $0$, and let $0\to M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M''\to0$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules. The localization $S^{-1}M$ is the module of fractions $m/s$, with $(m,s)\sim(m',s')$ exactly when some $t\in S$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$. Then
$$
0\longrightarrow S^{-1}M'\xrightarrow{S^{-1}f}S^{-1}M\xrightarrow{S^{-1}g}S^{-1}M''\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), with
subspaces as in [[def-subspace-topology-top]] and compactness as in
[[def-compact-space]]. Then:

1. **Closed in compact is compact.** If $(X, \mathcal{T})$ is compact and
   $F \subseteq X$ is closed in $X$, then $F$ is a compact subset of $X$.
2. **Finite unions.** If $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $K_0, \dots, K_n$ are compact
   subsets of $X$, then $K_0 \cup \dots \cup K_n$ is a compact subset of $X$. The
   union of the empty list is $\varnothing$, which is a compact subset of every
   space.

Claim 1 needs $X$ to be compact and claim 2 does not; no hypothesis of any kind
is placed on $X$ in claim 2. **No choice principle is used**: claim 1 selects
nothing, taking a least index where a selection would be natural, and claim 2
makes finitely many selections through [[lem-finite-choice]], a theorem of ZF.

Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g:X\to Y$ be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy $H:X\times[0,1]\to Y$. Then $f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)$ for every integer $n$. Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in $k$.

Assume AC. For a path-connected CW complex $X$ with a vertex basepoint, the
first Chern class induces a natural group isomorphism
$$c_1:\operatorname{Pic}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H^2(X;\mathbb Z),$$
where $\operatorname{Pic}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism
classes of numerable complex line bundles under tensor product. The same
statement holds for a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH space of CW
homotopy type.
citations.scope: At step 2.1, B_H=ET/H is path-connected paracompact Hausdorff CGWH of CW type by F4 and the quotient argument. The natural group isomorphism sends the trivial numerable line (the tensor unit) to zero. The explicit trivialization in step 2.1 supplies that line; pulling its zero integral class back and changing coefficients preserves zero. No classification theorem on the possibly non-CW subspace W is invoked.

citations.quote:
Assume AC. Let $L,M$ be numerable complex line bundles over a path-connected
CW complex with a vertex basepoint, or over a path-connected paracompact
Hausdorff CGWH space of CW homotopy type. Then
$$c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M),\qquad c_1(L^*)=-c_1(L),\qquad c_1(\overline L)=-c_1(L),$$
where $L^*$ is the dual line and $\overline L$ the conjugate line.
citations.scope: This is the second linked supplier recorded in Fact F5. Its Statement supplies tensor/dual/conjugate formulas for numerable lines on the same allowed base class under AC; it is auxiliary to the tensor-unit normalization. The decisive naturality and trivial-line zero used at step 2.1 come from the classification theorem, not a claim that these three displayed formulas alone classify bundles or prove a coefficient-change theorem.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume countable choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with its product Lie-group structure, and let $M$ be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let $a:T\times M\to M$ be a jointly smooth left action. Then $M$ admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under $a$. Its fixed set
$$
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
$$
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for each $p\in F$. The orthogonal normal bundle $\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F$ has no nonzero $T$-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of $F$, its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of $T$, with constant multiplicities; equivalently, $\nu_F$ admits a smooth $T$-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

Assume countable choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $g$ be a $T$-invariant Riemannian metric. If $S\subseteq M$ is a compact embedded $T$-invariant submanifold, its orthogonal normal bundle $
u(S)$ has a $T$-invariant open disk neighborhood $D_\epsilon(
u(S))$ of the zero section, and the normal exponential map is a $T$-equivariant diffeomorphism from that disk bundle onto a $T$-invariant open neighborhood of $S$. In particular, for $x\in M$, with stabilizer $H=T_x$, orbit $O=T\cdot x$, and normal fiber $V=
u_x(O)$, let $H$ act on $V$ by its differentials. There is an open $H$-invariant disk $D_\epsilon(V)$ such that $[t,v]$, the equivalence class of $(t,v)$ under $(t,v)\sim(th,h^{-1}v)$ for $h\in H$, maps by $[t,v]\mapsto t\cdot\exp_x(v)$ to a $T$-equivariant diffeomorphism from $T	imes_H D_\epsilon(V)$ onto an open neighborhood $U_x$ of $O$. Every stabilizer of a point in $U_x$ is a subgroup of $H$.

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ and use the product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$, $BT=ET/T$, with right diagonal action $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, put $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})$ is the degree-two class of the $i$th coordinate character line. For a smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$, set $L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi$, with the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. If $\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}$ for $\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r$, then $c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i$. Define $\mathscr S_T(k)$ to consist of $1$ and all finite products of $c_1(L_\chi)$ for nontrivial characters $\chi$. This is a multiplicative subset of $A_T(k)$ with $0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)$. For a topological space $X$ with a continuous left $T$-action, set $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$, with its $A_T(k)$-module structure induced by $ET\times_T X\to BT$. For an $A_T(k)$-module $N$, its localization $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N$ consists of fractions $n/s$, with $n\in N$, $s\in\mathscr S_T(k)$, and $n/s=n'/s'$ exactly when $u(s'n-sn')=0$ for some $u\in\mathscr S_T(k)$; addition is $(n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')$, and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)$. For $r=0$, there are no nontrivial characters and $\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}$.

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable manifold $M$ without boundary, let $F=M^T$, and use the product Milnor Borel construction with coefficients $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$. Let $\mathscr S_T(k)$ be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters of $T$. Then
$$
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M\setminus F;k)=0.
$$
Equivalently, every class in the Borel equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus is annihilated by some finite product of nontrivial character classes.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $S\subseteq R$ contain $1$, be closed under multiplication, and not contain $0$, and let $0\to M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M''\to0$ be an exact sequence of $R$-modules. The localization $S^{-1}M$ is the module of fractions $m/s$, with $(m,s)\sim(m',s')$ exactly when some $t\in S$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$. Then
$$
0\longrightarrow S^{-1}M'\xrightarrow{S^{-1}f}S^{-1}M\xrightarrow{S^{-1}g}S^{-1}M''\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact.

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and set $F=M^T$. Give the normal bundle $
u_F=(TF)^\perp$ the componentwise $T$-invariant complex orientation supplied by the fixed-locus normal-weight decomposition. Let $
u_{F,T}=ET	imes_T
u_F	o BT	imes F$ be its Borel vector bundle and let $e_T(
u_F)\in H_T^*(F;k)=H^*(BT	imes F;k)$, $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, be its zero-section Euler class. Then $e_T(
u_F)$ is a unit in $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(F;k)$. On each connected component $F_0\subseteq F$, restriction to $BT	imes\{p\}$, $p\in F_0$, is the product of the nontrivial character classes of the normal representation at $p$, with multiplicity and the chosen complex orientation.

For every subspace $A\subseteq X$ and abelian group $G$ there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{j}H^n(X;G)\xrightarrow{r}H^n(A;G)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^{n+1}(X,A;G)\to\cdots.$$
Here $j$ comes from including the relative cochains, $r$ is restriction, and the connector sends a cocycle class $[a]$ to $[\delta\widetilde a]$, for any cochain extension $\widetilde a$ of $a$ to $X$. Negative groups are zero, so the sequence begins $0\to H^0(X,A;G)\to H^0(X;G)\to H^0(A;G)$.

If $Z\subseteq A\subseteq X$ and $\overline Z\subseteq\operatorname{int}_X A$, inclusion induces an isomorphism
$$H^n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(X\setminus Z,A\setminus Z;G)$$
for every integer $n$ and every abelian coefficient group $G$.

Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g:X\to Y$ be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy $H:X\times[0,1]\to Y$. Then $f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)$ for every integer $n$. Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in $k$.

Assume AC. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then $BT\times F$ is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex $K$ such that $BT\times F\simeq BT\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Every open cover
of a paracompact Hausdorff space admits a locally finite partition of unity
subordinate to it.

Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal U$ be an open cover of $X$. A
family $\{\varphi_s:X\to[0,1]\}_{s\in S}$ is a **partition of unity** when each
$\varphi_s$ is continuous, the family of cozero sets
$\{\operatorname{coz}(\varphi_s)\}_{s\in S}$ is locally finite, and
$$\sum_{s\in S}\varphi_s(x)=1\quad\text{for every }x\in X.$$
The sum is unambiguous because local finiteness says that only finitely many
summands are nonzero near, and hence at, any fixed point.

It is **subordinate to $\mathcal U$** when for every $s\in S$ some
$U\in\mathcal U$ contains the support
$$\operatorname{supp}(\varphi_s):=\overline{\operatorname{coz}(\varphi_s)}.$$
Here cozero sets and zero sets have the meanings of
[[def-zero-sets-and-cozero-sets]].

Let $\xi=(E\xrightarrow\pi B,h)$ be a rank-$n$ real vector bundle equipped
with a continuous fiber metric.  Define
$$D_h(\xi)=\{v\in E:\|v\|_h\leq1\},\quad S_h(\xi)=\{v\in E:\|v\|_h=1\},$$
and define the Thom space by the based quotient
$$\operatorname{Th}_h(\xi)=D_h(\xi)/S_h(\xi).$$
Here $X/\varnothing$ means $X_+$, so the rank-zero convention is already
included.

For two supplied metrics $h$ and $k$, the canonical radial homeomorphism of
pairs is
$$r_{h,k}(0_b)=0_b,$$
$$r_{h,k}(v)=\frac{\|v\|_h}{\|v\|_k}v\quad(v\ne0).$$
It preserves the base and normalized radius, has inverse $r_{k,h}$, and
descends to the quotient.  Continuity at the zero section follows in a bundle
chart because the ratio of the two norms on the unit sphere is locally
bounded above and below.  The positive-definite interpolation
$h_t=(1-t)h+tk$ gives the canonical radial isotopy $r_{h,h_t}$.

This definition is choice-free once the metric is supplied.  For the empty
base all three spaces are empty except for the quotient basepoint; for rank
zero, $D_h(\xi)=B$, $S_h(\xi)=\varnothing$, and
$\operatorname{Th}_h(\xi)=B_+$.  The zero vector is fixed, sphere and disk
endpoints are preserved, and the formulas for $h=k$ are the identity.

Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\xi\to B$ be a metric rank-$n$ real
vector bundle.  Its **$R$-orientation local system** $\mathcal O_R(\xi)$ has
stalk
$$\mathcal O_R(\xi)_b=H^n(D(\xi_b),S(\xi_b);R).$$
On each bundle chart the fiber disk pairs identify with the standard disk
pair.  On overlaps, the linear transition functions induce units on its top
relative cohomology; these units are locally constant and satisfy the cocycle
law.  They therefore define a rank-one local system, whose path transport is
the corresponding composite of overlap units.  Metric changes give the same
system through the canonical radial pair isomorphisms.

The preceding disk-pair calculation identifies every stalk with a free
rank-one $R$-module.  An **$R$-orientation** is a section
$o=(o_b)$ of $\mathcal O_R(\xi)$ such that every $o_b$ generates its stalk;
equivalently it is a compatible locally constant family of fiber generators.
The bundle is **$R$-oriented** when such a section is supplied.

For $R=\mathbb F_2$, each one-dimensional stalk has exactly one nonzero
generator and every transition automorphism fixes it, so every real vector
bundle is canonically mod-two oriented.  Over $\mathbb Z$, a loop whose
monodromy sends a generator to its negative prevents an integral orientation:
compatibility would require $1=-1$ in $\mathbb Z$.

For rank zero the stalk is $H^0(*,\varnothing;R)=R$ and the unit gives the
standard orientation.  Empty bases have the unique empty section.  The zero
ring has its unique (zero) cyclic generator.  Identity and constant paths act
identically, reversed paths give inverse units, and no family of generators is
selected in making the definition.  It is choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly as in the general Thom theorem, and let
$\xi\to B$ be an $R$-oriented numerable real rank-$n$ vector bundle over a
base in the scope of that theorem. Let $u_\xi\in H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$ be its
normalized Thom class, let
$$j^*:H^n(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)\longrightarrow H^n(D(\xi);R)$$ be the relative-to-absolute map of the pair sequence, and let $s:B\to D(\xi)$ be the zero section. The **Euler class** of $\xi$ is $$e(\xi)=e_{\rm Th}(\xi):=s^*j^*(u_\xi)\in H^n(B;R).$$
This is the class already introduced in
[[def-thom-euler-class-of-an-oriented-vector-bundle]]: on this page we write
$e(\xi)$ for it, and the shorthand $s^*u_\xi$ always means the composite
$s^*j^*(u_\xi)$, the relative-to-absolute map being understood. For rank zero
with supplied orientation $o\in H^0(B;R)$, normalization gives $u_\xi=o$ and
$j$ and $s$ are identities, so
$$e(0_B,o)=o\in H^0(B;R).$$
In particular, the standard unit orientation gives $e(0_B,1)=1$.
For $R=\mathbb F_2$ every real bundle is canonically $\mathbb F_2$-oriented by
[[def-r-oriented-vector-bundle-and-orientation-local-system]], so in that
case $e_2(\xi):=e(\xi)\in H^n(B;\mathbb F_2)$ is defined for every real
bundle in the Thom scope; for $R=\mathbb Z$ the class depends on the chosen
integral orientation, and reversing the orientation negates it.

Assume AC and work over bases in the scope of the general Thom theorem. Let
$E\to B$ and $F\to B$ be $R$-oriented numerable real bundles of ranks $m,n\geq0$
with normalized Thom classes $u_E,u_F$ and Euler classes
$e(E),e(F)$. The coefficient ring $R$ is commutative and unital.
Every rank-zero input carries the standard unit orientation; the orientation
reversal assertion below applies only in positive rank. Both bases in a
pullback square are required to lie in the general Thom scope.

1. **Naturality.** For an orientation-preserving pullback square

   $$
   \begin{CD} f^*E @>>> E\\ @VVV @VVV\\ B' @>f>> B\end{CD}
   $$
   one has $e(f^*E)=f^*e(E)$.
2. **Orientation sign.** Over $R=\mathbb Z$ and $m>0$, reversing the orientation of $E$
   negates the class: $e(E,-o)=-e(E,o)$.
3. **Whitney product.** Give $E\oplus F$ the ordered direct-sum orientation.
   Then $e(E\oplus F)=e(E)e(F)$, including the rank-zero unit $e(0_B)=1$.
4. **Koszul sign.** The swap $E\oplus F\to F\oplus E$ changes the ordered-sum
   orientation by $(-1)^{mn}$. Consequently the Euler products in the two
   standard orders satisfy
   $$e(E)e(F)=(-1)^{mn}e(F)e(E).$$

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ and use the product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$, $BT=ET/T$, with right diagonal action $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, put $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\cong k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i=c_1(L_{\chi_i})$ is the degree-two class of the $i$th coordinate character line. For a smooth character $\chi:T\to S^1$, set $L_\chi=ET\times_T\mathbb C_\chi$, with the right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$. If $\chi=\chi_{\mathbf n}$ for $\mathbf n\in\mathbb Z^r$, then $c_1(L_\chi)=\sum_i n_i u_i$. Define $\mathscr S_T(k)$ to consist of $1$ and all finite products of $c_1(L_\chi)$ for nontrivial characters $\chi$. This is a multiplicative subset of $A_T(k)$ with $0\notin\mathscr S_T(k)$. For a topological space $X$ with a continuous left $T$-action, set $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$, with its $A_T(k)$-module structure induced by $ET\times_T X\to BT$. For an $A_T(k)$-module $N$, its localization $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}N$ consists of fractions $n/s$, with $n\in N$, $s\in\mathscr S_T(k)$, and $n/s=n'/s'$ exactly when $u(s'n-sn')=0$ for some $u\in\mathscr S_T(k)$; addition is $(n/s)+(n'/s')=(s'n+sn')/(ss')$, and scalar multiplication is induced by the localized ring. The character-localized Borel equivariant cohomology is $\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(X;k)$. For $r=0$, there are no nontrivial characters and $\mathscr S_T(k)=\{1\}$.

Assume countable choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with its product Lie-group structure, and let $M$ be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let $a:T\times M\to M$ be a jointly smooth left action. Then $M$ admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under $a$. Its fixed set
$$
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
$$
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for each $p\in F$. The orthogonal normal bundle $\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F$ has no nonzero $T$-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of $F$, its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of $T$, with constant multiplicities; equivalently, $\nu_F$ admits a smooth $T$-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

Assume AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $F=M^T$. For $k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}$, define $H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)$ using the product of the right Milnor circle models, let $A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)$, and let $\mathscr S_T(k)$ be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters $T\to S^1$. Then restriction along $i:F\hookrightarrow M$ induces a graded-ring isomorphism
$$
i^*:\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(F;k).
$$
The conclusion concerns compact finite-dimensional smooth $T$-manifolds and ordinary Borel singular cohomology; it makes no noncompact or compact-support assertion.

derivations.claim: A point \([z_0:z_1]\) is fixed by all \(t\in T\) only if one homogeneous coordinate is zero: if both were nonzero, equality \([z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1]=[z_0:z_1]\) would force \(e^{2\pi it}=1\) for every \(t\). Thus the fixed points are \(p_+\) and \(p_-\). In the local coordinate \(w=z_1/z_0\) at \(p_+\), the action is \(w\mapsto e^{2\pi it}w\). In \(v=z_0/z_1\) at \(p_-\), it is \(v\mapsto e^{-2\pi it}v\). These give the stated weights and character classes \(u\) and \(-u\), both inverted by \(\mathscr S_T(k)\). [F1, F2, algebra]

Since \(F\) is a pair of fixed points, \(ET\times_TF=(BT\times\{p_+\})\amalg(BT\times\{p_-\})\), so \(H_T^*(F;k)=A_T(k)\oplus A_T(k)\). Localizing this finite sum gives the displayed target, and [F3] identifies the restriction map with the asserted isomorphism. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

For a well-pointed topological group $G$ of CW type, the diagonal action on Milnor's $EG$ is free, $EG$ is contractible, and

$$ p:EG\longrightarrow BG $$

is a numerable principal $G$-bundle. The numeration satisfies the library's support-subordinate convention, not merely cozero containment.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the corresponding localizations. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define equivariant integration $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha$, the cohomological pushforward along those fibers; it lowers degree by $n$ and has values in $\mathcal R$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

Assume AC. Let $r\geq0$, let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ use the product Milnor model $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ with its ordinary product topology, and let $F$ be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then $BT\times F$ is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex $K$ such that $BT\times F\simeq BT\times K$.

For a well-pointed topological group $G$ of CW type, the diagonal action on Milnor's $EG$ is free, $EG$ is contractible, and

$$ p:EG\longrightarrow BG $$

is a numerable principal $G$-bundle. The numeration satisfies the library's support-subordinate convention, not merely cozero containment.

The embeddings

$$e\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i,\qquad o\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i+1$$

are $G$-equivariantly homotopic to the identity. If $a,b:T\to EG$ are
continuous equivariant maps, then
$(1-t)e(a(-))+t\,o(b(-))$ is a continuous equivariant homotopy.

For $G=S^1$ or $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the selected compact-group topology identifies $BG$ with the standard weak CW colimit of the finite projective quotients $\mathbb{CP}^N$ or $\mathbb{RP}^N$, respectively.

Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

This canonical composite is the Gysin map and is defined for every $\beta$ by the Thom isomorphism.

Pull the relative class in step 3.1 back along the zero section. By the definition of $e_T(
u)$ in [F1], the pulled-back Thom class is $e_T(
u)$, and pullback respects cup products. Hence $i^*i_*^T( eta)=e_T(
u)\smile eta$.

The Gysin class in step 3.1 is represented in a tubular neighborhood of $N$. Choose such neighborhoods disjoint for disjoint compact fixed components $N,N'$. The representative restricts to zero on $N'$, so $i_{N'}^*i_{N*}^T(\beta)=0$.

The fixed locus is closed in compact $M$, hence compact; its connected components are open in this locally connected manifold and compactness gives only finitely many.

The orthogonal complement of $(T_pM)^T$ in $T_pM$ is the normal fiber, so it contains no $T$-fixed vector. Averaging the representation against each character gives smooth projections onto the finitely many weight subbundles along each $F_j$.

u_j$ has nonzero weights, choose $X\in\mathfrak t$ outside the finite union of their kernels. > (Choice function).

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. derivations.claim: A point $[z_0:z_1]$ is fixed by every $\lambda$ precisely when it lies on one coordinate axis, so the fixed set is $\{p_0,p_\infty\}$. In the coordinate $w=z_1/z_0$ near $p_0$, the action is $w\mapsto\lambda w$, giving tangent weight $+1$; in $v=z_0/z_1$ near $p_\infty$, it is $v\mapsto\lambda^{-1}v$, giving weight $-1$. The complex orientations agree with $M$, so the Euler denominators are $u$ and $-u$.

The tautological fiber at $p_0$ is the trivial coordinate line, and at $p_\infty$ it is the weight-$+1$ coordinate line. Dualizing gives the fixed-fiber weights $0$ and $-1$ for $\mathcal O(1)$, hence $x|_{p_0}=0$ and $x|_{p_\infty}=-u$.
Substituting these restrictions and tangent Euler classes in [F2] gives $\int_M x=0/u+(-u)/(-u)=1$.

The linear functional $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ defines a section of $\mathcal O(1)$ that vanishes only at $p_\infty$. In the local coordinate $v=z_0/z_1$ and the dual tautological frame there, its coefficient is $v$, so its unique zero is transverse with positive local degree $+1$. Pulling the normalized Thom class back by a transverse section counts its isolated zeros with these local degrees: excision reduces the pairing to the degree of the section on the boundary of a small disk around each zero. Hence the ordinary Euler number is $1$. Restricting the Borel pushforward to the basepoint of connected $BT$ gives this ordinary Euler number, and $H^0(BT;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R$; therefore $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}x=1$, independently confirming the localized sum.

derivations.claim: The first-factor action fixes exactly $p_0=[1:0]$ and $p_\infty=[0:1]$, while it fixes every point of the second factor. Thus $M^T=F_0\sqcup F_\infty$, with each component a copy of $\mathbb{CP}^1$. The normal bundle is the tangent line of the first factor at its fixed point; in the coordinates $z_1/z_0$ and $z_0/z_1$ its weights are $+1$ on $F_0$ and $-1$ on $F_\infty$.

The normal complex line is the first factor and the fixed-component tangent space is the second. Moving the real two-dimensional first-factor orientation past the real two-dimensional second-factor orientation has sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$, so the induced component orientations agree with the product orientations.

The dual tautological fiber at $p_0$ has weight $0$ and at $p_\infty$ has weight $-1$, so the first-factor class restricts to $0$ and $-u$. Thus the contribution from $F_0$ is $0/u=0$; on $F_\infty$, the restricted class is $(-u)\eta$ and the normal Euler class is $-u$, leaving $\eta$, whose integral is $1$. On the first $\mathbb{CP}^1$, the section of $\mathcal O(1)$ induced by $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ has one positive transverse zero at $p_\infty$, so its Euler integral is $1$ by the normalized Thom-class zero count; the second-factor integral of $\eta$ is $1$ by definition. Assume countable choice. The negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform is continuous $\mathcal F:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$, and
$$\mathcal F(\partial^\alpha f)(\xi)=(2\pi i\xi)^\alpha\widehat f(\xi),\qquad \partial^\beta\widehat f=\mathcal F((-2\pi ix)^\beta f).$$

Assume countable choice. For every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\widehat f(\xi)e^{2\pi ix\cdot\xi}\,d\xi.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
