Use the dual $U(1)_D$ fields and potential of the preceding local
monopole-Higgs model. Let $x^1,x^2$ be coordinates on the transverse plane
$\mathbb R^2$ and let $x^3$ be the coordinate along a straight static tube.
Write $\widetilde A_i$ for the spatial dual gauge potential,
$\widetilde F_{12}=\partial_1\widetilde A_2-\partial_2\widetilde A_1$,
$D_iM=(\partial_i-i\widetilde A_i)M$, and
$D_i\widetilde M=(\partial_i+i\widetilde A_i)\widetilde M$.

A **finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding $n$** is a smooth static
configuration $(A_D,M,\widetilde M,\widetilde A_1,\widetilde A_2)$ on
$\mathbb R^2$ for which the transverse energy

$$\sigma=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{\widetilde F_{12}^2}{2g_D^2}+g_D^{-2}|\partial_i A_D|^2+|D_iM|^2+|D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_\mu-V_{\mathrm{vac}}\right)\,d^2x$$

is finite. The fields approach a supersymmetric vacuum at infinity satisfying
$A_D=0$, $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v>0$,
$\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(0)=0$, and
$V_{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. The phase map $M/|M|$ restricted to a sufficiently
large circle has degree $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ as a map to the unit
circle; the phase map $\widetilde M/|\widetilde M|$ has degree $-n$.
Require also that $D_iM$ and $D_i\widetilde M$ tend to zero on that circle,
that the coefficient of $d\theta$ in the pulled-back one-form $\widetilde A-d\arg M$ tends uniformly in
$\theta$ to zero as the circle radius tends to infinity, and that the
limiting flux exists. The profile is a translation-invariant
tube along $x^3$; its tension is the transverse integral $\sigma$. This
Definition includes no assertion that such a configuration exists or is a
stationary solution of the field equations.

In the adopted electric/magnetic frame, the **original electric flux** of
this sector means the dual magnetic flux
$\Phi_D=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x$.
The flux dictionary is part of the selected duality model; this Definition
does not state that every electric line charge is represented by a vortex.
In natural units, $[\widetilde A_i]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[\widetilde F_{12}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, and
$[\sigma]=\mathrm{mass}^2$.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local duality frame near one
monopole singularity of the selected pure $SU(2)$, four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ model. Let $A_D$ be the complex scalar coordinate in the
local dual $U(1)_D$ vector multiplet, and let $M,\widetilde M$ be complex
scalar fields of dual electric charges $+1$ and $-1$ in two $\mathcal N=1$
chiral multiplets. These are emergent infrared monopole fields in a dual frame of the independent pure ultraviolet model, not microscopic matter hypermultiplets. The dual gauge group acts by

$$A_D\mapsto A_D,\qquad M\mapsto e^{i\alpha}M,\qquad \widetilde M\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde M,\qquad \alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z).$$

Let $u(A_D)$ be the supplied holomorphic coordinate function on an open
patch $|A_D|<r$ about $A_D=0$, with $u(0)=u_m$ and
$c:=u'(0)\ne0$. Let $\mu\ne0$ be the coefficient of the small adjoint
mass perturbation, let $g_D>0$ be the dimensionless dual gauge coupling,
and use connection normalization for $A_D$, canonical kinetic terms for $M,\widetilde M$, and zero microscopic D-type Fayet--Iliopoulos parameter. Freeze the positive local vector-multiplet metric at $b=g_D^{-2}$; this is a specified constant-coupling two-derivative approximation within the patch, not the full field-dependent Wilsonian metric.
Define

$$W_\mu(A_D,M,\widetilde M)=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D),\qquad D=g_D\bigl(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2\bigr).$$

$$V_\mu=g_D^2|\partial_{A_D}W_\mu|^2+|\partial_M W_\mu|^2+|\partial_{\widetilde M}W_\mu|^2+\frac12D^2.$$

Let $\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu\widetilde A_\nu-
\partial_\nu\widetilde A_\mu$ and
$\widetilde D_\mu A_D=\partial_\mu A_D$,
$\widetilde D_\mu M=(\partial_\mu-i\widetilde A_\mu)M$, and
$\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M=(\partial_\mu+i\widetilde A_\mu)
\widetilde M$. In metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the
connection-normalized bosonic kinetic Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\eta^{\mu\nu}\left(g_D^{-2}\partial_\mu\overline{A_D}\,\partial_\nu A_D+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu M}\,\widetilde D_\nu M+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M}\,\widetilde D_\nu\widetilde M\right)-\frac{1}{4g_D^2}\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}\widetilde F^{\mu\nu}.$$

The mass dimensions are
$[A_D]=[M]=[\widetilde M]=[\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[u]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, $[W_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}^3$,
$[F_{A_D}]=[F_M]=[F_{\widetilde M}]=[D]=[\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$,
$[\widetilde A_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[c]=\mathrm{mass}$, and $[g_D]=1$. The allowed regime is restricted to
field values within this patch and energies below its stated effective
cutoff; “small $\mu$” means that the induced scale
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ lies well below that cutoff.

For a controlled leading linear-superpotential truncation, explicitly replace $u(A_D)$ by $u_m+cA_D$ in this constant-metric model. Then the perturbation is an $F$-type FI deformation of the local $\mathcal N=2$ abelian theory, related to a D-type FI deformation by rotation of its auxiliary triplet. This extra truncation admits the critical BPS square completion. The generic holomorphic $u(A_D)$ model above is softly broken to $\mathcal N=1$ and is not asserted to have exact BPS vortices; the full physical solution and a globally valid metric are separate inputs. Neither a small $\mu$ nor a holomorphic superpotential theorem alone controls all non-holomorphic metric or higher-derivative corrections.

This is a one-singularity effective data package. It includes neither a
simultaneously local electric description of mutually nonlocal dyons nor a
claim that the local action extends over the full moduli space. A finite-energy
vortex is not part of this Definition; its existence, when needed, is a
separate hypothesis.

derivations.claim:
In polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ write the smooth one-form
$\widetilde A=\widetilde A_r\,dr+\widetilde A_\theta\,d\theta$.
For a disk of radius $R$, integration of
$\widetilde F_{r\theta}=\partial_r\widetilde A_\theta-
\partial_\theta\widetilde A_r$ first in $r$ and then in $\theta$ gives
$\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x
=\int_0^{2\pi}\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)\,d\theta$: the
$\theta$-derivative term cancels by single-valuedness, and the inner
boundary term tends to zero because a smooth one-form has
$\widetilde A_\theta=O(r)$ at the origin.

On a sufficiently large circle choose a continuous phase
$M/|M|=e^{i\vartheta(\theta)}$ with
$\vartheta(2\pi)-\vartheta(0)=2\pi n$. The tangential condition in [F1]
implies $\widetilde A_\theta(R,\theta)-
\partial_\theta\vartheta(\theta)\to0$ uniformly in $\theta$ as
$R\to\infty$.
Taking the limit in step 1.1 therefore gives
$\Phi_D=\int_0^{2\pi}\partial_\theta\vartheta\,d\theta=2\pi n$.

Since $n\ne0$, step 2.1 gives nonzero flux, so the smooth function
$\widetilde F_{12}$ is nonzero at some point and hence on a neighborhood of
that point. Its squared integral is strictly positive. By [F2] and
$g_D>0$, the Maxwell term contributes strictly positive energy, while all
remaining energy terms are nonnegative; thus $\sigma>0$. Finiteness of
$\sigma$ is part of [F1]'s admitted-profile hypothesis.

A finite-energy profile of nonzero winding is an explicit hypothesis. Steps 1.1–3.1 derive its flux and positive tension; they never choose a profile from a class whose nonemptiness has not been established.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ in four-dimensional rigid, global
$\mathcal N=1$ gauge-model data. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex
Hermitian vector space of scalar field values, let a compact Lie group $G$ act
unitarily on $V$, and fix an orthonormal complex basis
$(\phi^1,\ldots,\phi^n)$ of $V$. Choose Hermitian matrices
$T_a$ for the infinitesimal action of a basis of the Lie algebra of $G$, a
gauge coupling $g>0$, and a gauge-invariant holomorphic polynomial
$W:V\to\mathbb C$. Assume canonical scalar kinetic energy and no
Fayet--Iliopoulos term. Define the auxiliary-field maps

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\sum_i\partial_\mu\overline{\phi^i}\,\partial^\mu\phi^i,\qquad [\phi^i]=\mathrm{mass},\quad [W]=\mathrm{mass}^3,\quad [g]=1.$$

$$F_i(\phi)=\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi^i}(\phi),\qquad D_a(\phi)=-g\,\phi^\dagger T_a\phi.$$

The tree-level scalar potential is

$$V_{\mathrm{tree}}(\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n|F_i(\phi)|^2+\frac12\sum_a D_a(\phi)^2.$$

Thus $F_i$ and $D_a$ have mass dimension two and $V_{\mathrm{tree}}$ has
mass dimension four.

A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar
configuration $\phi\in V$ for which every $F_i(\phi)$ and every
$D_a(\phi)$ is zero. Its **classical vacuum-moduli set** is the topological
orbit space

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{\phi\in V:F_i(\phi)=0\text{ for all }i,\ D_a(\phi)=0\text{ for all }a\}/G.$$

where two configurations are identified exactly when they lie in the same
compact-$G$ orbit, and the set has the quotient topology. The stability
convention here retains every such compact-group orbit, including singular
orbits. No quotient by the complexified group, geometric-invariant-theory
stability criterion, or smooth-manifold structure is included in this
definition.

For a **specified, already constructed quantum theory** $\mathcal T$, suppose
there is a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary translation representation
$U(a)$, and densely defined supercharges $Q^I$ and their Hilbert adjoints on a
common domain $\mathcal D$. A **quantum supersymmetric vacuum ray** is the
phase-equivalence class $[\Omega]$ of a normalized vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$
satisfying
$U(a)\Omega=\Omega$ for every spacetime translation $a$ and
$Q^I\Omega=(Q^I)^*\Omega=0$ for every supercharge $I$. The **quantum
vacuum-moduli set** $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$ is the set of these
rays, with the topology, if any, supplied by the constructed theory. This
definition is conditional on normalizable invariant vacuum vectors and a
specified quantum Hilbert-space model. It asserts no path-integral measure,
continuum limit, nonperturbative existence, or equality between
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$.

derivations.claim:
Since $W=0$, both holomorphic derivatives vanish identically, so every
$(q,\widetilde q)$ is F-flat. The D equation is
$-g(|q|^2-|\widetilde q|^2)=0$; because $g>0$, it is equivalent to
$|q|=|\widetilde q|$. By [F1], the classical vacuum set is exactly that
D-flat set modulo the displayed U(1) action.

The product $m=q\widetilde q$ is invariant under the action, since
$(e^{i\alpha}q)(e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde q)=q\widetilde q$. It therefore
defines a map from the D-flat orbit set to $\mathbb C$.

For any $m_0\in\mathbb C$ with $m_0\ne0$, choose
$q=\sqrt{|m_0|}>0$ and $\widetilde q=m_0/q$. Then
$q\widetilde q=m_0$ and $|q|=|\widetilde q|=\sqrt{|m_0|}$; for
$m_0=0$, choose $(q,\widetilde q)=(0,0)$. Thus every $m_0$ is attained by
a D-flat pair.

If two D-flat pairs have the same product $m_0=0$, their equal-modulus
condition forces both pairs to be $(0,0)$. If $m_0\ne0$, both $q$-entries
are nonzero and have modulus $\sqrt{|m_0|}$; hence their ratio is a phase
$e^{i\alpha}$, and equality of products forces the corresponding
$\widetilde q$-entries to differ by $e^{-i\alpha}$. The two pairs are
therefore U(1)-gauge-equivalent. The map in step 2.1 is injective as well
as surjective, proving the stated bijection.

patch $|A_D|<r$ about $A_D=0$, with $u(0)=u_m$ and

mass perturbation, let $g_D>0$ be the dimensionless dual gauge coupling,

Let $\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu\widetilde A_\nu-
\partial_\nu\widetilde A_\mu$ and
$\widetilde D_\mu A_D=\partial_\mu A_D$,
$\widetilde D_\mu M=(\partial_\mu-i\widetilde A_\mu)M$, and
$\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M=(\partial_\mu+i\widetilde A_\mu)
\widetilde M$. In metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the
connection-normalized bosonic kinetic Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\eta^{\mu\nu}\left(g_D^{-2}\partial_\mu\overline{A_D}\,\partial_\nu A_D+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu M}\,\widetilde D_\nu M+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M}\,\widetilde D_\nu\widetilde M\right)-\frac{1}{4g_D^2}\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}\widetilde F^{\mu\nu}.$$

$[A_D]=[M]=[\widetilde M]=[\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[u]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, $[W_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}^3$,
$[F_{A_D}]=[F_M]=[F_{\widetilde M}]=[D]=[\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$,
$[\widetilde A_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,

field values within this patch and energies below its stated effective
cutoff; “small $\mu$” means that the induced scale

$\mathcal N=1$ gauge-model data. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex
Hermitian vector space of scalar field values, let a compact Lie group $G$ act
unitarily on $V$, and fix an orthonormal complex basis
$(\phi^1,\ldots,\phi^n)$ of $V$. Choose Hermitian matrices
$T_a$ for the infinitesimal action of a basis of the Lie algebra of $G$, a
gauge coupling $g>0$, and a gauge-invariant holomorphic polynomial
$W:V\to\mathbb C$. Assume canonical scalar kinetic energy and no
Fayet--Iliopoulos term. Define the auxiliary-field maps

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\sum_i\partial_\mu\overline{\phi^i}\,\partial^\mu\phi^i,\qquad [\phi^i]=\mathrm{mass},\quad [W]=\mathrm{mass}^3,\quad [g]=1.$$

$$F_i(\phi)=\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi^i}(\phi),\qquad D_a(\phi)=-g\,\phi^\dagger T_a\phi.$$

The tree-level scalar potential is

$$V_{\mathrm{tree}}(\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n|F_i(\phi)|^2+\frac12\sum_a D_a(\phi)^2.$$

Thus $F_i$ and $D_a$ have mass dimension two and $V_{\mathrm{tree}}$ has
mass dimension four.

A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar
configuration $\phi\in V$ for which every $F_i(\phi)$ and every
$D_a(\phi)$ is zero. Its **classical vacuum-moduli set** is the topological
orbit space

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{\phi\in V:F_i(\phi)=0\text{ for all }i,\ D_a(\phi)=0\text{ for all }a\}/G.$$

where two configurations are identified exactly when they lie in the same
compact-$G$ orbit, and the set has the quotient topology. The stability
convention here retains every such compact-group orbit, including singular
orbits. No quotient by the complexified group, geometric-invariant-theory
stability criterion, or smooth-manifold structure is included in this
definition.

$U(a)$, and densely defined supercharges $Q^I$ and their Hilbert adjoints on a
common domain $\mathcal D$. A **quantum supersymmetric vacuum ray** is the
phase-equivalence class $[\Omega]$ of a normalized vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$
satisfying

$Q^I\Omega=(Q^I)^*\Omega=0$ for every supercharge $I$. The **quantum

definition is conditional on normalizable invariant vacuum vectors and a
specified quantum Hilbert-space model. It asserts no path-integral measure,
continuum limit, nonperturbative existence, or equality between

derivations.claim:
Differentiating $W_\mu=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D)$ gives
$F_{A_D}=\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(A_D)$,
$F_M=\sqrt2 A_D\widetilde M$, and
$F_{\widetilde M}=\sqrt2 A_DM$. At $A_D=0$, the first equation is
$\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu c=0$, while the other two vanish.

Set $v=(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}>0$ and
$\widetilde M=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v)$, with $M=v$. Then
$M\widetilde M=-\mu c/\sqrt2$ and
$|\widetilde M|=|\mu c|/(\sqrt2v)=v$, so all F equations and
$D=g_D(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2)=0$ hold.

Any solution in this patch with $A_D\ne0$ would have
$M=\widetilde M=0$ by the last two F equations, contradicting
$\mu u'(A_D)\ne0$ in the first. Thus $A_D=0$; the first F equation fixes
the nonzero product and the D equation fixes equal magnitudes. The U(1)
phase can then make $M=v$ and fixes $\widetilde M$ as in the Example, so
the solution is one gauge orbit.

Expanding the canonical kinetic terms around $M=v$ and
$|\widetilde M|=v$, and canonically normalizing
$\widetilde A_c=\widetilde A/g_D$, gives
$m_D^2=2g_D^2(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2)=4g_D^2v^2>0$. This verifies the
local Higgs mass only; it supplies no vortex solution.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

A **finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding $n$** is a smooth static
configuration $(A_D,M,\widetilde M,\widetilde A_1,\widetilde A_2)$ on
$\mathbb R^2$ for which the transverse energy

$$\sigma=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{\widetilde F_{12}^2}{2g_D^2}+g_D^{-2}|\partial_i A_D|^2+|D_iM|^2+|D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_\mu-V_{\mathrm{vac}}\right)\,d^2x$$

$A_D=0$, $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v>0$,
$\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(0)=0$, and
$V_{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. The phase map $M/|M|$ restricted to a sufficiently
large circle has degree $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ as a map to the unit
circle; the phase map $\widetilde M/|\widetilde M|$ has degree $-n$.
Require also that $D_iM$ and $D_i\widetilde M$ tend to zero on that circle,
that the coefficient of $d\theta$ in the pulled-back one-form $\widetilde A-d\arg M$ tends uniformly in
$\theta$ to zero as the circle radius tends to infinity, and that the
limiting flux exists. The profile is a translation-invariant
tube along $x^3$; its tension is the transverse integral $\sigma$. This
Definition includes no assertion that such a configuration exists or is a
stationary solution of the field equations.

In the adopted electric/magnetic frame, the **original electric flux** of
this sector means the dual magnetic flux
$\Phi_D=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x$.
The flux dictionary is part of the selected duality model; this Definition
does not state that every electric line charge is represented by a vortex.
In natural units, $[\widetilde A_i]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[\widetilde F_{12}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, and
$[\sigma]=\mathrm{mass}^2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ on $\mathbb C$ with distinct centers and positive integer multiplicities; let $N=\sum_jm_j$. There is a unique real scalar function $h$, smooth on $\mathbb C\setminus\{z_j\}$, such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across each center, $h\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$, and
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j}$$
in distributions, where $\langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)$ for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$. For $N>0$, $h<0$ off the divisor; for the empty divisor, $h=0$. With $P(z)=\prod_j(z-z_j)^{m_j}$, $s=2\log|P|$, and the orientation $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$, the fields
$$q(z)=\sqrt\xi\,e^{(h(z)-s(z))/2}P(z),\qquad A=-\tfrac12 *d(h-s)$$
extend smoothly across the centers and solve $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, where $D_A=d-iA$ and $B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2=dA$. They have finite energy
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2$$
and flux $\int_{\mathbb R^2}B\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi N$. For every $0<\alpha<\sqrt\kappa$ and every multi-index $\beta$, $|\partial^\beta h(z)|=O(e^{-\alpha|z|})$ as $|z|\to\infty$; the curvature $B$ and covariant gradient $D_Aq$ have the same exponential decay. On the exterior of a disk, the local gauge $e^{-i\arg P}$ gives $q_{\mathrm{ext}}=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A_{\mathrm{ext}}=-\tfrac12 *dh$, so the fields approach the vacuum exponentially in that exterior gauge; the raw global representative $q$ need not have an exponentially small phase correction. Negative winding $-N$ is obtained by complex conjugation and $A\mapsto-A$, with flux $-2\pi N$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ and use the critical Abelian-Higgs energy and boundary-sector convention in which $D_A=d-iA$, $B=dA$, $q$ tends in modulus to $\sqrt\xi$, and its exterior phase has winding $n\in\mathbb Z$. For every smooth finite-energy field pair $(A,q)$ in that sector,
$$E(A,q)\ge 2\pi\xi|n|.$$
For $n\ge0$, the exact identity is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{(B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2))^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2+2\pi\xi n;$$
for $n\le0$, replace $D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2}$ by $D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2}$ and $B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ by $B+e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, with topological term $-2\pi\xi n$. The boundary-current term in the disk identity vanishes along a radius sequence derived from the finite-energy hypotheses. The fields reconstructed for any fixed divisor by the arbitrary-divisor plane theorem attain equality, are absolute transverse energy minima in their winding sector, have zero first variation under smooth compactly supported variations, and have nonnegative second variation in those directions. This does not assert uniqueness of minimizing fields across distinct divisors of the same degree.

$$\mathcal E_L(\mathcal A,q)=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left[\frac{B_{12}^2+F_{31}^2+F_{32}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+|D_3q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right]dx_1dx_2dz,$$

$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{0\le z\le L}\left|\int_{\partial D_R}(A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2-n\,d\theta)\right|=0$$
and zero radial magnetic-flux leakage, meaning that the integral of $F$ over the side $\partial D_R\times[0,L]$ tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. If their exterior phase is $n\theta+\phi_j$, first apply the globally smooth degree-zero gauge cleanup proved below and prescribe the resulting representatives as the end values. In particular the neutral scalar lies in the specified small closed disk, the positive smooth **light-hyper-retaining** metric has the explicit bounds $b_-,b_+$, the vacuum approach is uniform, and theta is omitted or constant. $$t_*=\min\{\xi/2,m_*/\sqrt2\}>0,\qquad C_V=\max\left\{\frac{4b_+\xi^2}{m_*^2},\;6b_++\frac{2K^2}{t_*}\right\},\qquad c_V=C_V^{-1},\qquad \gamma=\min\left\{1,\frac{b_-}{b_0},2b_0c_V\right\}>0.$$

$$V_b\ge c_V(s-\xi)^2,\qquad E_b\ge\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|.$$

$$0<\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty.$$

Any two such canonical representatives admit a smooth fixed-width finite-energy interpolation collar in the same winding class; the collar keeps the neutral scalar in its convex disk. In particular, for fixed end traces $P_0,P_1$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there are finite constants $C_\varepsilon$, $\ell>0$, independent of $L$, such that for $L\ge2\ell$

$$\tau_nL\le I_n(L;P_0,P_1)\le(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon.$$

Therefore

$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{I_n(L;P_0,P_1)}{L}=\tau_n>0.$$

This is asymptotically linear classical confinement of the specified original electric flux in the stated local magnetostatic boundary model. It does not assert that the planar infimum or finite-cylinder infimum is attained, that a nonlinear stationary profile is BPS, or that $I_n(L)=\tau_nL+O(1)$. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Put $x=\sqrt2M\widetilde M$ and $U_0=\mu c$, so $s^2=d^2+2|x|^2$ and $\xi=\sqrt2|U_0|$. By the fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment from $0$ to $a$ inside the convex disk, $|\mu(u'(a)-c)|\le K|a|$. If $s\le t_*$, then $|x|\le s/\sqrt2\le m_*/2$, whereas the disk hypothesis gives $|\mu u'(a)|\ge m_*$. Hence $|H|\ge m_*/2$ and $V_b\ge m_*^2/(4b_+)\ge[m_*^2/(4b_+\xi^2)](s-\xi)^2$, since $s\le t_*\le\xi/2$. If $s\ge t_*$, the reverse triangle inequality in $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb C$ gives $(s-\xi)^2\le d^2+2|x+U_0|^2\le d^2+4|H|^2+4K^2|a|^2$. The three terms are bounded by $2b_+V_b$, $4b_+V_b$, and $2K^2V_b/t_*$, respectively, because $V_b\ge2|a|^2s\ge2t_*|a|^2$. Combining the cases proves the stated uniform potential bound without a Hessian or minimizer assumption.

Use the unitary real-linear change $q=(M+e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$, $p=(M-e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$; both fields have charge +1 and $s=|q|^2+|p|^2$. Their summed covariant-gradient norms equal the original charged norms. Let $E_0$ be the critical two-charge functional with terms $b_0B^2/2+|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)$ and no additional p-mass term. The Maxwell bound $b\ge b_-$, step 1.1 and the definition of $\gamma$ give $E_b\ge\gamma E_0$, after dropping the nonnegative neutral gradient. In particular $E_0$ is finite. Uniform vacuum approach makes q,p bounded near infinity, with $|q|\to\sqrt\xi$ and $p\to0$ in the vacuum phase frame. Stokes on disks and the original angular condition give limiting flux $2\pi n$.

Write $G(R)=\int_{|x|=R}(|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2)\,ds$. Finiteness of the gradient integral implies $\int_{R_0}^{\infty}G(R)\,dR<\infty$. There are radii $R_j\to\infty$ with $R_jG(R_j)\to0$: otherwise $G(R)\ge\epsilon/R$ eventually for some $\epsilon>0$, contradicting that integral. By [F3] and bounded tail amplitudes, the absolute boundary-current integral $\oint(\bar qDq+\bar pDp)$ on these circles is at most $C\sqrt{R_jG(R_j)}\to0$. For $n>0$, expand the disk square identity using $[D_1,D_2]f=-iBf$ for $f=q,p$: $|(D_1+iD_2)f|^2=|Df|^2-B|f|^2+i\{\partial_1(\bar fD_2f)-\partial_2(\bar fD_1f)\}$ and $b_0[B-b_0^{-1}(\xi-s)]^2/2=b_0B^2/2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)+Bs-\xi B$. Add the identities, integrate, and let $R_j\to\infty$. The boundary current vanishes along this subsequence, the flux tends to $2\pi n$ and the remaining squares are nonnegative, so $E_0\ge2\pi\xi n$. Reflection of the second transverse coordinate proves $E_0\ge2\pi\xi|n|$ for negative n. Step 2.1 now proves the claimed positive bound for every full-model profile. No full-circle boundary-current limit was assumed or inferred from finite energy.

Let $N=|n|$. Choose smooth radial functions f,h with f(r) equal to a positive constant times $r^N$ near zero, h(r) equal to a constant times $r^2$ near zero, and f=h=1 outside one fixed disk; choose the near-zero coefficients as smooth functions of $r^2$ and interpolate on a compact annulus. Set $q=\sqrt\xi f(r)e^{in\theta}$, $p=a=0$, and $A=nh(r)d\theta$, hence $M=q/\sqrt2$, $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$. The charged fields are smooth at zero because $r^Ne^{in\theta}$ is $z^N$ or $\bar z^N$, and the connection is smooth because $r^2d\theta=x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1$. Curvature and every non-vacuum energy term are supported in a fixed disk; all are smooth there. Outside it the field is exactly in the vacuum orbit, the covariant gradients vanish and the angular flux coefficient is n. Thus this is an admitted finite-energy profile. Its energy is positive by step 3.1 and finite directly; consequently $0<\gamma2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty$.

For any profile, M is nonzero outside a disk by uniform vacuum approach. The circle-valued function $(M/|M|)e^{-in\theta}$ has degree zero on that exterior annulus. It has a smooth real phase lift $\chi$: the closed real one-form $-if^{-1}df$ for this circle-valued function f has zero integral on each circle, so integrating first radially and then angularly from a fixed base point defines a smooth periodic lift with $e^{i\chi}=f$. Multiply $-\chi$ by a radial smooth cutoff equal to zero near the inner boundary and one on a larger exterior annulus, then exponentiate to obtain a globally smooth gauge transformation. The transformed fields have $M=m e^{in\theta}$, m>0, and $A=nd\theta+\alpha$ outside a compact set. This gauge change leaves energy and the original angular condition invariant and fixes the exact exterior M-phase; it does not impose a new decay hypothesis. Write $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}w e^{-in\theta}$, so m,w tend uniformly to v.

On this exterior, s is bounded below by $\xi/2$ and m by $v/2$. The potential controls $|a|^2\le V_b/\xi$, $d^2\le2b_+V_b$, $|H|^2\le b_+V_b$ and $(s-\xi)^2\le C_VV_b$. Since $m^2-v^2=(s+d-\xi)/2$, $|m-v|^2\le[(s-\xi)^2+d^2]/(2v^2)$ is integrable. Also $m w-v^2=e^{-i\beta}[H-\mu(u'(a)-c)]/\sqrt2$, so $|w-v|\le(2/v)\{(|H|+K|a|)/\sqrt2+v|m-v|\}$ is square-integrable. Thus a,m-v,w-v are in $L^2$ on the exterior. Finally $DM=e^{in\theta}(dm-im\alpha)$, with dm and alpha real. Its squared norm is $|dm|^2+m^2|\alpha|^2$, so finite charged energy and m>=v/2 give $\alpha,dm\in L^2$. On compact sets all fields and coefficients are smooth and bounded. Hence any two canonical profiles differ in $L^2$ in a,M,$\widetilde M$ and their connection one-forms. These mass-tail conclusions use uniform approach to the vacuum as well as the finite potential/kinetic energy; finite energy alone was not asserted to force pointwise vacuum approach.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The selected classical model is the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills model with spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and global gauge group $G=SU(2)$ rather than $SO(3)$. Its field data are one $SU(2)$ connection, six real adjoint scalars, and four adjoint Weyl fermions, with the coupling and action normalization fixed by the selected model data. The gauge coupling $g>0$ is dimensionless in four dimensions. The model's sixteen-supercharge invariance is adopted as part of that classical model; this definition does not add a proof of invariance, a quantum measure, or a continuum construction.

A four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal field theory (SCFT) is, by definition here, a unitary positive-energy quantum field theory whose local-operator state space carries the four-dimensional conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$ together with its $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal extension. The real Lie superalgebra for the selected maximally supersymmetric case is $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$: it is the real form of the supertrace-zero $4|4$ matrix Lie superalgebra preserving a Hermitian form with signature $(2,2)$ on the even block and positive signature on the odd block, modulo its central real line $\mathbb R\,iI_{4|4}$; for a block-diagonal matrix $A\oplus D$, the supertrace is $\operatorname{tr}A-\operatorname{tr}D$. Its even part is $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(4)_R$, with $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$; its odd generators are the Poincar\'e supercharges $Q,\bar Q$ and the special superconformal charges $S,\bar S$. The conformal generators include translations $P_\mu$, Lorentz transformations $M_{\mu\nu}$, dilations $D$, and special conformal transformations $K_\mu$. A superconformal primary is a state annihilated by all $K_\mu$ and all special superconformal charges; its descendants are obtained by applying $P_\mu$ and Poincar\'e supercharges. A unitary representation means that these generators act on a common invariant dense domain, the indicated adjoints are Hilbert adjoints, translations and radial Hamiltonian are self-adjoint, and the inner product is positive.

For the scalar-primary sector, use the selected $\mathcal N=1$ subalgebra and normalize its $U(1)_R$ generator $R$ so that the three adjoint chiral superfields have scalar charge $2/3$. Write $d_{\mathcal O}$ for the eigenvalue of the dilation generator on a scalar superconformal primary $|\mathcal O\rangle$ and $r_{\mathcal O}$ for its $R$ charge. The scalar unitarity bound in this convention is $d_{\mathcal O}\geq 3|r_{\mathcal O}|/2$; equality in the positive-charge branch is the chiral-primary shortening condition. The local conditional norm argument is given by the chiral-primary unitarity item on this page; no classification of all $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$ representations is asserted here.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

For the index sector require the closed odd operator $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ to be self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed composition equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply a simultaneous orthonormal energy/charge/parity eigenbasis for $\delta,J_1',\ldots,J_k'$ and $(-1)^F$, with real eigenlabels $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ and maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains. Here $\lambda\ge0$, the joint labels form a supplied countable set, and entire gap eigenspaces, including the protected kernel, may be infinite-dimensional. For every joint projection $P$, require $P D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP\psi=PT\psi$ for $T=Q,S,D_Q$ on $D(T)$. These reducing-domain conditions specify the actual spectral compatibility; common-domain commutators alone are insufficient. The grading preserves the joint subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains.

For $\beta>0$ and finite real or complex chemical potentials $\boldsymbol\mu$, define the weighted exponential first on the finite joint-eigenvector span by the eigenvalues $\exp(-\beta\lambda+\sum_a\mu_a j_a)$. Require its closure to be bounded trace class for every $\beta>0$ at the chosen $\boldsymbol\mu$. This is the meaning of the exponential in the index observable, not an unspecified product of unbounded operators. Every joint block then has finite dimension: its weight is nonzero and infinitely many equal singular values would violate trace class. Infinite total gap multiplicities are permitted through infinitely many joint blocks. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta,\boldsymbol\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H(S^3)}\left((-1)^F\exp\left[-\beta\delta+\sum_{a=1}^k\mu_aJ_a'\right]\right).$$

If the trace is not trace class, the same symbol may be used only for a specified formal series whose coefficients are defined; it does not denote a convergent partition function. The index is called protected against $\beta$-variation when the stated operator and trace hypotheses imply that positive-$\delta$ states cancel in the graded trace, as proved by the index-pair theorem on this page. A source's further claim of invariance under changing a coupling requires its own stated deformation hypotheses. A protected local operator means a named primary whose dimension is fixed by a specified shortening relation; the word alone asserts no deformation invariance.

For the quantum coupling family, use the source normalization

$$\tau=\frac{\theta}{2\pi}+\frac{4\pi i}{g^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0,$$

This is the physical component coupling family, not the formal Wilsonian coordinate $\tau_{\mathrm h}$ of the earlier zero-theta density bridge; no equality of the two parameter symbols is inferred. Here, on a closed oriented Euclidean four-manifold $X$ with an $SU(2)$ bundle, $k=-\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)\in\mathbb Z$ is the instanton number in the selected trace convention and $\theta$ weights its sectors by $e^{i\theta k}$. For the opposite, positive-ASD counting convention $k_{\mathrm A}=+\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)/(8\pi^2)$ on the same oriented manifold, one has $k_{\mathrm A}=-k$ by definition. The fixed physical gauge coefficient gives weight $q^k$ for a positive self-dual sector and $\bar q^{k_{\mathrm A}}$ for a positive anti-self-dual sector on the real coupling slice, where $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$. A local ADHM/Nekrasov pole orientation and weight identification is separate data; it is not obtained by equating these signed charge symbols. The corresponding source-reported $S$ and $T$ parameter maps are $S:\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$ and $T:\tau\mapsto\tau+1$. The global form and line-operator spectrum are part of the theory data, not determined by the Lie algebra alone. In the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ center-charge sector define $\mathcal C=\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ with charge $(e,m)$ and mutual-locality pairing

$$\langle(e,m),(e',m')\rangle=em'-me'\pmod 2.$$

An electric Wilson line is parallel transport traced in a representation of the global gauge group; a magnetic 't Hooft line is specified by a magnetic singularity around the support curve; a dyonic line carries both charges. Their center-charge classes are $(e,m)\in\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$. An allowed center-charge set is a subgroup $L\subseteq\mathcal C$ on which the displayed pairing vanishes; the three maximal such subgroups are the line-spectrum data for $SU(2)$, $SO(3)_+$, and $SO(3)_-$. The source-reported charge maps are $S:(e,m)\mapsto(m,-e)$ and $T:(e,m)\mapsto(e+m,m)$, so these transformations may change the global form. The 2007 and 2013 sources read for this item describe the quantum $S$-duality as a conjecture and refine it by global form and line data. This dated source status is recorded as such; this item does not assert an exhaustive literature-status review, an open-problem classification, or a proof of equivalence between the theories.

derivations.claim: For a block $b$ with $\lambda_b>0$, let $K_b=(Q+S)|_{\mathcal H_b}$. The actual adjoint/domain and reducing-block hypotheses make this an everywhere-defined odd self-adjoint finite-dimensional operator. Since $Q^2=S^2=0$ and $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$, $K_b^2=\lambda_b I/2$. Thus $B_b=\sqrt{2/\lambda_b}K_b$ is a unitary odd involution exchanging the two block parity spaces. This uses this page's supercharge normalization, not the differently normalized right-handed charge on the index page.

The restriction $U_b$ commutes with $K_b$. Its even and odd restrictions are therefore unitarily conjugate by $B_b$ and have equal finite traces. The signed contribution from this block, including its common heat factor, is zero. The full weighted operator is trace class by [A1], so its basis diagonal is absolutely summable; regrouping by the countable blocks preserves the sum. Only zero-gap blocks contribute, even if infinitely many blocks share a gap.

For $\psi\in\ker\delta$, the exact closed anticommutator relation on its domain gives $0=2(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|S\psi\|^2)$, hence $Q\psi=S\psi=0$. Conversely a vector in both charge kernels lies in both composition domains and has $\delta\psi=0$. The restriction of the trace-class heat-weighted operator to this kernel is just $U$, so its signed trace converges absolutely and contains no $\beta$. This proves the stated identity and includes an infinite protected kernel whenever the insertion makes its trace convergent.

derivations.claim: Using $S|\mathcal O\rangle=0$ and the Hilbert-adjoint relation, [F1] gives $(d_{\mathcal O}-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{S,Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Thus $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O}$, with equality exactly when $Q|\mathcal O\rangle=0$.

The conjugate anticommutator similarly gives $(d_{\mathcal O}+\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|\bar Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Combining the two inequalities gives $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\max(\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O},-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})=\tfrac32|r_{\mathcal O}|$; the active equality condition is the first norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\geq0$ and the conjugate norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\leq0$.

derivations.claim: The three nonzero elements of $\mathcal C$ are $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(1,1)$. Each generates an order-two subgroup with the origin. The pairing is alternating, so each such subgroup is isotropic. Any subgroup containing two distinct nonzero elements contains two linearly independent columns in $\mathbb Z_2^2$; the determinant $em'-me'$ of two independent columns is nonzero and therefore equals $1$ in $\mathbb Z_2$. Hence such a subgroup is not isotropic. Therefore these are exactly the three maximal isotropic subgroups, and [F2] gives their source-reported gauge-group labels.

Modulo $2$, the map $S$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(0,1)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,0)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(1,1)$. The map $T$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,1)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(0,1)$. These invertible linear maps therefore send the displayed subgroups exactly as stated. Their coupling transformations and physical interpretation as dualities are the source-reported conjectural inputs [F2], not consequences of the finite arithmetic.

Define the degree-six invariant polynomial

$$\mathcal I_6(\rho,A_\rho):=2\pi\left[\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}\exp\!\left(-\frac{iF_\rho}{2\pi}\right)\right]_6=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}(F_\rho\wedge F_\rho\wedge F_\rho),$$

This is a homogeneous polynomial in the formal curvature; on a four-dimensional physical spacetime it is interpreted on the formal six-dimensional extension used for descent, not integrated as a six-form over spacetime. Define the horizontal differential $d_H:=dx^\mu D_\mu$; its square is $d_H^2a=dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu D_\mu D_\nu a=\tfrac12dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu[D_\mu,D_\nu]a=0$. Extend $s$ to horizontal forms by $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge sa$. Since $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$, one has $s(d_Ha)=-dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu(sa)=-d_H(sa)$, hence $sd_H+d_Hs=0$.

For $p=0$, set $\mathcal A_U^{g,-1}=\{0\}$. The local BRST cohomology modulo total derivatives in bidegree $(g,p)$ is

$$H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p}:\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_U^{g+1,p-1}\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_U^{g-1,p},\ n\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p-1}\}}.$$

The denominator is a subspace of the numerator: for $a=sm+d_Hn$, choose $b=sn$ and compute $sa+d_Hb=s^2m+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. For $p=0$, $n=b=0$ and the same verification reduces to $s^2m=0$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Consequently $sI_5+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$ yields the physical convention $\delta I_5=d_H\mathcal E^4(I_4^{(1)})$.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. We quotient by all such finite-jet local counterterms and by compactly supported total derivatives; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i))$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, where $SU(3)=\{g\in M_3(\mathbb C):g^\dagger g=I_3,\det g=1\}$ and $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For a finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho:H\to U(V_\rho)$, let $A_\rho$ be a smooth anti-Hermitian matrix-valued one-form on a smooth manifold $X$, representing a connection in a local trivialization, and set $F_\rho=dA_\rho+A_\rho\wedge A_\rho$. Define the degree-six invariant polynomial

$$\mathcal I_6(\rho,A_\rho):=2\pi\left[\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}\exp\!\left(-\frac{iF_\rho}{2\pi}\right)\right]_6=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}(F_\rho\wedge F_\rho\wedge F_\rho),$$

where the exponential is its formal power series and $[\,\cdot\,]_6$ selects the differential-form component of degree six. This is a homogeneous polynomial in the formal curvature; on a four-dimensional physical spacetime it is interpreted on the formal six-dimensional extension used for descent, not integrated as a six-form over spacetime. The normalization fixes anti-Hermitian generators, the fundamental trace, and the overall coefficient once and for all.

For the defining representation $E=\mathbb C^3$ with $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, a background connection is $A_E=A+iB I_3$, where $A$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(3)$-valued one-form and $B$ is a real $U(1)$ connection one-form. The dual representation is $E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C)$ with $\rho_{E^*}(g,z)=\rho_E(g,z)^{-T}$; its induced connection and curvature are $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_E^T$.

Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

Let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal-form spaces on a smooth open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, with nilpotent BRST differential $s$, horizontal differential $d_H$, and $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

A **finite groupoid** is a small category in which every morphism is invertible, with finitely many isomorphism classes and a finite automorphism group at every object. Write $\pi_0(\mathcal C)$ for its set of isomorphism classes. Its **groupoid cardinality** is

$$|\mathcal C|:=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For an isomorphism-invariant function $f:\pi_0(\mathcal C)\to\mathbb C$, define

$$\int_{c\in\mathcal C} f(c):=\sum_{[c]\in\pi_0(\mathcal C)}\frac{f(c)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(c)|}.$$

For finite groupoids $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, a functor $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$, its **homotopy fiber** $\mathcal C_d$ has objects $(c,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:p(c)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}d$ and morphisms $u:(c,\alpha)\to(c',\alpha')$ satisfying $\alpha'\circ p(u)=\alpha$. Define pullback and pushforward of invariant functions by

$$(p^*g)([c])=g([p(c)]),\qquad (p_!f)([d])=\int_{(c,\alpha)\in\mathcal C_d} f([c]).$$

A span $\mathcal X\xleftarrow{a}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal Y$ of finite groupoids therefore induces the linear map $b_!a^*$ on invariant functions.

Assume full AC. Give the unit sphere $S^4\subset\mathbb R^5$ its boundary orientation, round metric and standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball. Let $S=S^+\oplus S^-$ be its complex spinor bundle, with skew-Hermitian Clifford action $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$ and positive chirality the $+1$ eigenspace of $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. A spin lift here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ bundle double-covering the oriented orthonormal frame bundle; explicitly $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)\times Sp(1)$ covers $SO(4)$ by $(a,b):q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group, identified with $SU(2)$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$.

The twisted chiral Dirac operator $D^+_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$ is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.

Assume full AC and use the explicit round spin sphere, $E=S^+$ connection, Clifford action and chiral Dirac operator of the round-sphere spin-twist lemma. $$

$$

Equivalently, gluing the gauge fibers by $z=-1$ with an antiperiodic spin clutch gives periodic total spinor boundary conditions; gluing by $z$ with periodic spin clutch gives antiperiodic total boundary conditions instead. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $E_R=P\times_R V_R$ be the associated Hermitian bundle. Let $S^+$ and $S^-$ be the associated bundles of the two half-spin representations of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. The chiral Dirac operator is the first-order operator

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),$$

where $H^1$ and $L^2$ are the first Sobolev and square-integrable completions for the fixed Riemannian metric. Assume the operator is Fredholm. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

Here $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$, including $\det0=\mathbb C$. Our phrase **inverse determinant line** means the dual of $\Delta_A=\det\ker D^+\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}D^+)^*$; the displayed $\mathcal L$ is the line called $\mathrm{Det}$, not $\mathrm{Det}^{-1}$, in Dai–Freed §2. This explicit formula fixes the convention throughout.

The named regularized geometry means the following supplied **admissible analytic data**, rather than an arbitrary Hermitian line relabeled by a name. Test smooth dependence on each finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ of connections on the fixed $M,P,R$. Write $\mathscr H^\pm=T\times L^2(M;S^\pm\otimes E_R)$ with common first-Sobolev domains. Supply unitary parameter connections $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ on these Hilbert bundles, preserving smooth sections and the Sobolev domains; for the fixed product identification one may take the ordinary derivative in $T$. Fix a positive inverse-length scale $\mu$ and put $\mathscr D=D^+/\mu$, with Hilbert adjoint $\mathscr D^*$. These choices and the local-counterterm convention are fixed before phases are compared.

Require $Q^+=\mathscr D^*\mathscr D$ and $Q^-=\mathscr D\mathscr D^*$ to have the supplied nonnegative self-adjoint realizations with discrete spectrum, finite multiplicities and smooth eigensections, and the same positive spectrum with multiplicity. A spectral cut is a number $a>0$ not in either spectrum on an open parameter patch $U_a\subseteq T$. The orthogonal projections onto eigenvalues $\lambda<a$, including zero modes, must form smooth finite-rank bundles $V_a^\pm\subset\mathscr H^\pm$; their complements are denoted $\mathscr H^\pm_{>a}$. The finite cut line is $L_a=(\det V_a^+)^*\otimes\det V_a^-$. For $a<b$, the operator $\mathscr D$ is invertible between the eigenbundles $V_{(a,b)}^+$ and $V_{(a,b)}^-$. Glue $L_a$ to $L_b$ by tensoring with its top exterior power $\det\mathscr D_{(a,b)}$. Finite-dimensional cancellation of these invertible modes identifies each fiber with the displayed kernel/cokernel line, even where kernel dimensions jump. Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. No existence of that continuation for an arbitrary Fredholm family is inferred.

Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. On the invertible complement let $\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a}=\widetilde\nabla^-_{>a}\mathscr D_{>a}-\mathscr D_{>a}\widetilde\nabla^+_{>a}$. For $t>0$ define the complex one-form $h_a(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathscr H^+_{>a}}(\mathscr D_{>a}^{-1}(\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a})e^{-tQ^+_{>a}})$; the trace is the absolutely convergent sum of diagonal matrix coefficients in an orthonormal eigenbasis, independent of choices within each eigenspace. Gauge identifications must intertwine all cut data, preserve this norm and preserve the connection after the corresponding parameter pullback. These are explicit mathematical conditions on the supplied regularization. Cut gluing reduces on a finite band to the determinant derivative $(\det\mathscr D)^{-1}\nabla(\det\mathscr D)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D^{-1}\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D)$ with the induced finite-dimensional connections; analytic existence, smooth heat expansions and naturality for all geometric families are not asserted here. Smooth gluing, the square identification, spectral continuations, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are required Pfaffian admissibility data, not an arbitrary choice of a square root or an existence assertion for every real/pseudoreal theory.

More generally, let a nonempty compact closed oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold have a smooth unitary $SU(2)$ rank-two twist and a Fredholm chiral Dirac realization with $n_+=\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+$ and $n_-=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+$. Let $z=-I$ be the central gauge automorphism of $E$. On the inverse chiral determinant line

$$

The spin convention is part of the statement: using antiperiodic spinors in the circle direction gives no product zero mode. This distinguishes the tested fermion-parity mapping-torus convention from an automatic eta-holonomy formula. No general spectral-flow or Atiyah–Singer theorem is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
