only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. A section $s$ of a rank-$d$
bundle $Q$ is a **regular section** here if, at each point of its zero scheme
$Z(s)$, some local frame expresses $s$ by $d$ components forming a regular
sequence of length $d$ in the local ring. Under this hypothesis it has exact
Koszul resolution
$\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$.
Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a
finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting
injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and
resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth
quasi-projective varieties $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, let $E$ be a finite
locally free sheaf on $X$. The strict transform
$F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$
restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to
$P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.

For an additive left-exact functor $F$ and a bounded-below complex $K$ with supplied Cartan–Eilenberg resolution $I$, there is a spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^qF(K^p)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb R_I^{p+q}F(K),\qquad d_r:(p,q)\mapsto(p+r,q-r+1).$$
Here $q\ge0$ and $p\ge b$ if $K^p=0$ for $p<b$. It is first quadrant after translating $p$ by $b$ and converges strongly with a finite filtration on every target degree. Derived objects use the supplied columns; under DC, or supplied Cartan–Eilenberg comparison and homotopy data, it is natural in $K$ and independent of the resolution from $E_1$ onward.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$X=\mathbb P^n_k$ with dualizing line bundle $\omega_X=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ and
residue trace $t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$
([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]), and let
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}$ be the global sheaf Ext of
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]].

1. **(The pairing.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$
   and $\eta\in H^q(X,F)$ set
   $$\langle\alpha,\eta\rangle_F\;:=\;t_X\Bigl(\chi^n_{\omega_X}\bigl(\alpha\cdot\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)\bigr)\Bigr),$$
   where $\chi^q_F:\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,F)$
   is the canonical isomorphism of
   [[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]],
   $\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$ is the corresponding class in
   $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)$, and
   $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)$
   is the Yoneda product of
   $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$ with
   $\beta=\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$, i.e. composition
   $\alpha\circ\beta$ of derived morphisms under
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))}(-,-[\bullet])$
   ([[thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category]],
   [[prop-yoneda-product-is-composition-in-the-derived-category]]). This
   **Serre duality pairing** is $k$-bilinear and natural in $F$.

2. **(Perfectness.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ and every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ the pairing
   $$\langle-,-\rangle_F:\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\times H^q(X,F)\longrightarrow k$$
   is a perfect pairing of $k$-vector spaces, i.e. both adjoint maps
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^q(X,F)^\vee$ and
   $H^q(X,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)^\vee$ are
   isomorphisms.

The case $q=n$ of clause 2 is the classical statement that
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^n(X,F)^\vee$,
$\varphi\mapsto(\eta\mapsto t_X(H^n(\varphi)(\eta)))$, is an isomorphism, and
for $F=\mathcal O_X$ clause 2 recovers $H^{n-q}(X,\omega_X)\cong H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)^\vee$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field, let $Y$ be a nonsingular equidimensional quasi-projective
$k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), let $n\ge0$ and let
$$p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\longrightarrow Y$$
be the projection. For every
$\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(p_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;p_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY})\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd
class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $p_!$ is the K-theory
pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]],
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) and $p_*$ is the proper
pushforward on Chow groups
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently, writing
$\tau_X(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)_{\mathbb Q}\\ \downarrow p_! & & \downarrow p_*\\ K_0(Y) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\end{array}$$
commutes. The case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for
$\mathbb P^n$, and the case of a general projective-bundle projection is obtained
by the same argument applied to the projective bundle formula.

Let $m \ge 1$, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^m$ be a nonempty connected open set,
and let $f : U \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). If there is a
nonempty open set $W \subseteq U$ such that $f(z) = 0$ for every $z \in W$, then
$f \equiv 0$ on $U$.

This is the several-variable identity theorem at the strength the page supports:
the hypothesis is a nonempty **open** set of zeros. An accumulation point of the
zero set is neither assumed nor sufficient in several variables; the companion
page records that stronger one-variable statement as false here.

derivations.claim: The Ward construction gives exactly the smooth pullback bundle and vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator required in [A1], for the same sphere and incidence in [F1]. Thus its two cohomology vanishings apply directly. The dual is again unitary and ASD, since its curvature is $-F_A^t$ and Hodge star commutes with transpose, and its holomorphic operator is the induced dual one. Hence both $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))$ and $H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))$ vanish. This uses the supplier's exact stated conclusion, not an unexposed injective-map premise.

Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$.

Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty complex-open subset of the line family of $P$. Choose affine coordinates $(x,y)$ with the original line given by $y=0$. This open family contains the projective lines $y=b$ for all sufficiently small complex $b$, so their union contains a nonempty open subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on each such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$. It therefore vanishes on that open subset. In a connected coordinate chart and holomorphic bundle frame, [F8] makes its zero-germ locus closed as well as open. The plane is connected (any two points lie on a connected projective line), so the section vanishes everywhere; no density assertion for an arbitrary complex-open line family is needed. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$.

Tensor $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ by $\mathcal E$. Step 1.2 gives $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=0$, and step 1.1 gives $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. The long exact sequence yields $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$. Serre duality and step 1.1 also give $H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring the second factor by $\mathcal E(-2)$, pushing to the first factor, and twisting that output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal construction resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ before the output twist and $\mathcal E$ after that twist; it is concentrated in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. Its only cohomology is the degree-zero hypercohomology of the diagonal resolution, namely $\mathcal E$; the first and last terms are exact because the other total degrees vanish. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Thus this is the stated monad; its cohomology vector spaces are canonical, and changing bases acts by $GL(U)\times GL(K)\times GL(U')$.

From [A3], $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E(t))=Ne^{tH}-kH^2e^{tH}$ and $\operatorname{td}(T_Z)=1+2H+\tfrac{11}{6}H^2+H^3$. Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch [F7] gives $\chi(\mathcal E(t))=N\binom{t+3}{3}-k(t+2)$, with values $k,-N+2k,0,-k$ for $t=-3,-4,-2,-1$. The Euler sequences $0\to\mathcal O(-4)\to\mathcal O(-3)^{\oplus4}\to\Omega_Z^2\to0$ and $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ give Euler characteristics $k,2k+N,k$ for the three monad coefficient bundles. Steps 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 leave only $H^2$ in each, so these values are the dimensions.

The space of parallel sections of $\widehat E$ evaluates to a trivial subbundle, and its orthogonal complement is parallel because the connection is unitary. No nonzero parallel section lies in the complement. Every flat summand is trivial since $S^4$ is simply connected [F2]. The Ward transform and diagonal construction preserve direct sums. For a trivial rank-$m$ summand $\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}$, the two Euler sequences and [F6] give coefficient groups $H^2(\mathcal O(-3))=0$, $H^2(\Omega_Z^2)^{\oplus m}\cong\mathbb C^m$, and $H^2(\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$, so its monad is $0\to\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}\to0$. Flat summands are therefore included without imposing $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$ or $H^0(Z,\mathcal E^\vee)=0$. No Dirac index or kernel-dimension formula is used.

boundaries.evidence: Proof 5.1 includes trivial flat summands: each contributes U=U'=0 and a middle O^m term. In particular at k=0, Proof 4.2 gives outer dimensions zero and middle dimension N; empty outer coefficient spaces do not erase the nonempty real-line family or impose H^0(E)=0.
Statement; steps 4.1, 4.2 and 5.1: k=0 allows zero end terms, while constant flat summands stay in the middle term and are treated separately.
Statement; step 4.2: The dimensions k,2k+N,k include k=1; framing rank remains the exact upstream Ward range.
Statement; steps 1.1, 2.1 and 5.1: Both bundle/dual coupled vanishings are used, the complex-open line family supplies an open zero set, and flat summands are retained.

boundaries.reason: This reconstruction has no FI parameter or chamber-limit assertion; its charge and projective-family qualifications are explicit hypotheses.

boundaries.evidence: Statement; steps 3.1 and 4.1: The declared AC/DC and exact diagonal/cohomology/family suppliers remain in force; no nonzero H0 assumption is used to discard a flat summand.

boundaries.reason: The lemma reconstructs a monad from a Ward bundle and does not itself state a two-way matrix classification.
Inverse raw matrix normalization and U(k) uniqueness are supplied separately, not inferred from this monad construction.

citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $k\ge0$ and
$N\ge2$. On $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with homogeneous coordinates
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, set
$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2) =(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1), \qquad \sigma([z])=[jz].$$
For each $(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, let $\ell_z$ be the real twistor line
defined by
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$
and let $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Suppose
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta} \mathcal O(1)\otimes U'$$
is a complex of holomorphic vector bundles with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split
injective and surjective end maps, and locally free middle cohomology
$F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of rank $N$, where
$\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$ and
$\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Suppose $F|_{\ell_z}$ is holomorphically trivial for
every $z$, and it has a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing
whose induced first-slot-linear Hermitian form on
$H^0(\ell_z,F|_{\ell_z})$ is positive definite for every $z$. Here the
pairing means an isomorphism $h:F\to D(F)$ fixed by $D$, where for a
homogeneous linear matrix $P$ one sets $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and the signed
dual monad has differentials $-\beta^\#$ and $\alpha^\#$; thus $D^2$ is the
identity under the induced double-dual identifications. Suppose also that a
unitary framing identifies $F|_{\ell_\infty}$ isometrically with
$W\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for a fixed Hermitian space $W$ of dimension
$N$.

Then there are Hermitian
spaces $V$ and $W$ of dimensions $k$ and $N$, with $W$ carrying the prescribed
framing, and maps
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V),\qquad I:W\to V,\qquad J:V\to W$$
such that, after a pairing-preserving framed chain identification, the monad
maps are
$$\alpha= \begin{pmatrix} A\\ C\\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),$$
where
$$A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\qquad C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2.$$
The extracted maps satisfy both zero-moment equations
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$
They are stable, meaning the vectors
$B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, and costable, meaning no nonzero
subspace invariant under both $B_i$ is contained in $\ker J$. Conversely,
every such regular datum with both moments zero gives a locally split monad
with the stated real-line positivity and infinity framing.
Here $\dagger$ denotes adjoint in the indicated Hermitian spaces.

In the next assertion, a normalized framed isomorphism is a chain
isomorphism preserving the lifted pairing and the specified infinity frame.
Such isomorphisms correspond exactly to the simultaneous $U(V)$ action
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\longmapsto (gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V).$$
Thus inverse coefficient extraction recovers precisely one $U(V)$ orbit; when
$k=0$, $U(0)$ is trivial, and every constant flat summand is retained as an
unused orthogonal subspace of $W$.

For $t_1,t_2\in U(1)$, choose an orthonormal framed basis
$w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $W$ and phases $e_1,\ldots,e_N\in U(1)$, and let
$h(w_a)=e_a^{-1}w_a$. The coordinate action
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto
(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ acts on data by
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto (t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
The corresponding chain factors on the source, middle and target terms are,
respectively,
$(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, and $1$.

The same extraction and classification hold naturally for first-order
families over $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with
$\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$ in the following exact locally-free/base-change
range: the three modules are free of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, the end maps are
locally split, the middle cohomology is locally free and commutes with
reduction, its global section module is free and commutes with reduction, the
coefficient-image submodule in the middle term is a direct summand and
commutes with reduction, and each fixed real-line restriction is trivial
with its section module commuting with reduction. The framing and pairing
are defined over $A$, while positivity is required only on the reduced
complex; adjoints on these modules use the coefficient involution and the
induced $A$-Hermitian forms. Call an $A$-valued datum regular when its
reduction is stable and costable. The extracted matrices lie over $A$ and
obey the same moment equations. Conversely, every $A$-valued regular datum
whose raw
monad satisfies these same global-section, coefficient-image and real-line
base-change conditions gives a family in this range. Pairing-preserving
framed family isomorphisms correspond exactly to
$U(k,A)=\{g:g^\dagger g=1\}$. This assertion is restricted to reduction and
the involution-preserving base maps $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ with
$r\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite algebraic monad resolution, let
$H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ and
$H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$. The hyperplane cycle
map identifies these classes in their respective theories. Then
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$ and
$c_2^{\rm alg}(F)=kH_{\rm alg}^2$. Its topological line class is the same
$H_{\rm top}$ and $c_2^{\rm top}(F)=kH_{\rm top}^2$. Identify
$\mathbb P^3$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ through
the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the $\ell_z$ and
$\ell_\infty$, and let $\pi:\mathbb P^3\to S^4$ be its projection. Give each
fiber its complex orientation, orient $S^4$ so that the positive incidence
chart followed by the fiber orientation is the complex orientation of
$\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class.
For this positive twistor orientation, $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$; consequently, if the underlying
topological bundle is $\pi^*E$ for a bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then
$c_2(E)=ku$.

Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Use the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing input stated below for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the cohomology of a linear monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

The reconstructed monad in [F1] is linear with locally free middle bundle, trivial on every real line, and has the positive Hermitian Ward pairing and unitary framing fixed in the definition. Its dimensions are those required by [A1]. Thus, assuming the exact supplier [A1], extract the raw tuple from its intrinsic normal form. Its monad composition vanishes, so [F5]'s polynomial identity makes both raw moment coefficients zero. Full fiber rank on each real line and [F5]'s Gram/rank equivalence identify the locus exactly with stable-and-costable regularity. The intrinsic unitary normalization and inverse-extraction clause in [A1] identify the remaining framed monad changes precisely with $(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ for $g\in U(k)$. Conversely, the regular raw monad in [F5] is a global holomorphic bundle, trivial on every real line, with canonical positive reality: its pairing is induced by the standard Hermitian form on K and β(v)=α(σv)*. It is well-defined on cohomology since kerβ(v) is orthogonal to imα(σv), and on a real line its canonical representatives are kerD with the positive restricted metric; at infinity it is W. The normalization of [F3] with determinant reduction [F4] gives k=c₂(E)[S⁴]=−q_N. Under [A1], extraction and construction are inverse on U(k) orbits and framed Ward connections, proving the full claim under the exact normal-form, GAGA and coupled-vanishing hypotheses stated above.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

For $n=2$ or $3$, let $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ and let $X^{an}$ be its complex analytic space and $\eta:X^{an}\to X$ the canonical morphism of ringed spaces. Define analytification on $X^{an}$ by $\mathcal F^{an}=\eta^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\eta^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves. It identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms, preserves cohomology and the derived morphism groups $\operatorname{Ext}^q$, and commutes with restriction to the fixed hyperplane $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$. For an algebraic coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ flat over a finite-type complex parameter scheme $S$, let $p:X\times S\to S$ be projection. Analytification commutes with the algebraic family structure and fiber restrictions. Whenever the algebraic and analytic higher direct images $R^qp_*\mathcal E$ are locally free and the natural maps from their residue-field fibers to $H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$ are isomorphisms, the comparison identifies those direct images and base-change maps. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

Assume full AC and the exact projective GAGA comparison used below. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by the positive holomorphic reality pairing is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let a framed real Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ have the normalized linear monad with vector-space dimensions $k,2k+N,k$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

The tuple is regular exactly when the associated quaternionic construction is pointwise nondegenerate. Its kernel projection connection extends over $\infty$, has the specified framing, and equals the Ward connection. Changes of normalized monad bases induce exactly the $U(k)$ action on raw data, and inverse matrix extraction recovers the same $U(k)$ orbit. The resulting charge is $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. The entrywise conjugation candidate is refuted by the recorded comparison lemma and is not used in the intrinsic real monad normalization.

Let $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,P,Q)$ obey the source equations stated in the following references section. Under the proposed substitution

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ source solution in the proof below.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. derivations.claim: By [A1], each regular zero-FI unitary orbit determines one regular complex $GL(k)$ orbit, and each regular complex orbit has exactly one balanced unitary representative. The two constructions are inverse because each orbit intersection is unique; the quotient map is a diffeomorphism in the word-frame charts. The exact torus action in [F1] commutes with both gauge actions, so this quotient identification is $T$-equivariant.

By [A2], every stable complex orbit gives one framed torsion-free $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf with the stated rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial, and the converse recovers the same orbit. Its locally-free locus is exactly the costable locus. Thus restricting [A1]'s complex quotient to regular orbits gives exactly that locally-free sheaf locus; the positive-FI stable quotient still contains the non-locally-free boundary. The family and first-order version is conditional on [A2]'s displayed base-change hypotheses and [A3], so no tangent claim is inferred outside that range.

Starting with a framed ASD connection, [A4] constructs its holomorphic Ward bundle; the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing and diagonal argument [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]] reconstructs the normalized three-term monad. Starting with regular ADHM data, [A5] identifies its normalized real monad and projection connection with this Ward bundle and connection. The equality of the two constructions is the first-order and inverse-extraction clause in [A5], so it is conditional on that exact real block proof, not on the P² citation alone.

By [A5], both composites on framed isomorphism classes are identities: ADHM data produce the Ward bundle whose monad extraction returns the same $U(k)$ orbit, and an ASD connection produces a Ward bundle whose matrix extraction returns an orbit reconstructing that framed connection. The charge of each resulting connection is $q_N=-k$ by [F2]–[F3]. Thus the claimed bijection and charge statement follow conditionally on [A4]–[A5].

The finite-dimensional quotient and $\mathbb P^2$ sheaf maps are $T$-equivariant by [A1]–[A2]. The Ward construction is natural under rotations and framing transformations by [A4]; the exact raw monad torus factors are directly calculated in the new block lemma cited by [A5], while the equivariance of inverse normalization remains part of [A5]. These exact interfaces make the composite $T$-equivariant. The same composition on first-order families is valid only under the base-change hypotheses of [A2]–[A4] and the deformation compatibility of [A5]. This proves the stated conditional torus and tangent clauses and leaves the positive-FI boundary separate.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=v^*w$ and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with Riemannian metric $g_X$. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B$ be a positive-definite, symmetric, $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$-invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak g$. For any local section $s_i$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. Invariance of $B$ makes the local four-forms $\beta_B|_{U_i}=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ and $\gamma_B|_{U_i}=B(F_i\wedge *_{g_X}F_i)$ restrictions of global forms. Define $q_B=\int_X\beta_B$. For a real scalar $g>0$, define the Euclidean Yang–Mills functional by

$$
S_B(P,\omega):=\frac{1}{g^2}\int_X\gamma_B,
$$

where the Hodge operator is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Then

$$
S_B(P,\omega)\geq \frac{8\pi^2}{g^2}\,|q_B(P,\omega)|.
$$

Equality holds exactly in these cases: if $q_B>0$, then $F_i=*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B<0$, then $F_i=-*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B=0$, then $F_i=0$. Every self-dual or anti-self-dual supplied connection satisfies the source-free Euclidean Yang–Mills equation $D_{A_i}(*_{g_X}F_i)=0$, where $D_{A_i}\eta=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The statement asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a connection in any charge sector.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

derivations.claim: When $k=0$, $V=0$. There is exactly one quadruple of maps, all with zero-dimensional domain or codomain. Both moment equations are the unique equality of endomorphisms of $0$; the span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists. Thus this datum is stable and costable, and the quotient by $U(0)$ is one point.

For the framed ASD connection, $q_B=q_N=0$ by [F2], so the ASD action bound gives $F_A=0$. For two piecewise smooth paths from $\infty$ to $x$, their concatenation is a loop and is null-homotopic by [F3]. Pull back a cover by coordinate balls with local parallel frames to the compact homotopy square; a Lebesgue number gives a finite subdivision with each cell mapped into one such ball. Transport along a continuous edge is defined using that ball's parallel frame; on overlaps the change between parallel frames is constant, so the definition is independent of the chosen ball. Each cell has identity boundary transport, and multiplying over the subdivision cancels all interior edges. Therefore the loop holonomy is identity and transport from $\infty$ is path-independent. The resulting sections of a framed orthonormal basis are smooth and parallel in local parallel frames, so the bundle with connection is framed-isomorphic to the trivial bundle with its flat connection. The framing fixes that isomorphism at $\infty$. Any covariantly constant unitary automorphism preserving the framing is identity, since its value at every point is its parallel transport from the identity at $\infty$. Thus the framed flat gauge class is unique and has no residual based stabilizer.

The conditional correspondence of [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]] sends the unique zero-dimensional datum to this unique framed flat ASD class and preserves $q_N=0$. This verifies the $k=0$ boundary without an irreducibility assumption.

Proof 1.1 checks k=0 explicitly: V=0, unique maps, vacuous stability/costability and quotient by U(0) a point. Proof 1.2 uses q_N=0 and ASD to force F_A=0 and constructs the unique framed flat class.

The zero-dimensional ADHM quotient has exactly one element by Proof 1.1, not a rank-one framing space. The Example quantifies N>=2 and k=0, so N=1 and charge k=1 are outside this example's stated range.

Proof 1.1 gives the unique empty datum explicitly. Proof 1.2 transports the fixed framed orthonormal basis from infinity and proves path independence using simply connected S4 and local parallel frames; this is a canonical construction rather than a choice of gauge representative in every sector.

Proof 1.2 uses the ASD zero-charge implication q_N=0 -> F_A=0, then the framing and path-independent transport identify the input with the trivial flat connection. Thus every member of the stated zero-charge sector is that framed flat class.

The trivial framed flat connection has F_A=0, hence is ASD and its trace-curvature integral gives q_N=0. It therefore lies in the stated sector; Proof 2.1 matches it to the unique empty datum under the conditional correspondence.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. $$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

derivations.claim: For $V=W=\mathbb C$, both commutators vanish. Thus $\mu_{\mathbb C}=IJ=0$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}=|I|^2-|J|^2=\zeta$. Since $I\ne0$, the words of length zero applied to $I(W)$ span $V$, so the datum is stable. Since $J=0$, the nonzero subspace $V$ is invariant and contained in $\ker J$, so the datum is not costable; in particular it is not a zero-FI regular datum. By [F2], its positive-FI complex orbit has a representative with $I=1$ after the $GL(1,\mathbb C)$ change of basis $g=\zeta^{-1/2}$.

Substituting that representative in [F3] gives $\alpha=(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T$ and $\beta=(z_2,-z_1,z_0)$. Their product is $-z_2z_1+z_1z_2=0$. The row $\beta$ is surjective at every projective point because its three entries have no common zero, and $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map because it is nonzero away from $p$. Let $K=\ker\beta$. Projection to the third coordinate restricts to a morphism $\gamma:K\to\mathcal O$. On the affine chart $z_0=1$, put $x=z_1$ and $y=z_2$; a vector in $K$ has the form $(u,v,-yu+xv)$, so $\gamma(K)=(x,y)$ and its kernel is generated by $(-x,-y,0)$, the image of $\alpha$. On any chart away from $p$ where $z_1$ or $z_2$ is a unit, the same equations show that $\gamma$ is onto and its kernel is generated by $\alpha$. Hence $K/\operatorname{im}\alpha\cong I_p$ globally, where $I_p$ is the ideal sheaf of $p$.

At $p$, the local ideal $(x,y)$ is not principal: if it were generated by one element in the regular local ring $\mathbb C[x,y]_{(x,y)}$, its quotient by the maximal ideal would have dimension at most one, whereas $(x,y)/(x,y)^2$ has dimension two. Therefore $I_p$ is not locally free at $p$. Its framing on $L_\infty$ is the canonical trivialization because $p\notin L_\infty$. This exhibits a positive-FI stable point outside the costable, locally-free zero-FI locus; the correspondence with ordinary ASD moduli is restricted to that zero-FI locus and does not absorb this boundary point.
