$\mathcal U$ with values in $\mathcal F$** by
$$C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p} \mathcal F\bigl(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}\bigr),$$
the product of the section groups over all increasing $(p+1)$-tuples
$i_0<\cdots<i_p$ in $I$; write an element as $s=(s_{i_0\cdots i_p})$. For
$p<0$ put $C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=0$. When $I$ has no increasing
$(p+1)$-tuple the product is empty and $C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$; when an
intersection $U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ is empty, the corresponding
factor is the one-element group $\mathcal F(\varnothing)=0$
([[lem-sheaf-section-over-empty-set-terminal]]).

The **Čech differential** $\delta^p:C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to
C^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is defined on an increasing $(p+2)$-tuple
$i_0<\cdots<i_{p+1}$ by
$$(\delta^p s)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}} =\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j\, s_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_j}\cdots i_{p+1}} \Big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{p+1}}},$$
where $\widehat{i_j}$ means that the index $i_j$ is omitted and the restriction
is taken from $U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\widehat{U_{i_j}}\cdots\cap U_{i_{p+1}}$ to the
full intersection ([[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]). For $p<0$
set $\delta^p:=0$. The maps $\delta^p$ are group homomorphisms, componentwise
sums of restrictions, so the data $(C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F),\delta^p)_{p\in
\mathbb Z}$ form a cochain complex of abelian groups; that $\delta^{p+1}\circ
\delta^p=0$ is proved in [[lem-cech-differential-squares-zero]]. The pair
$(\mathcal F,\mathcal U)$ being fixed, the construction is functorial in
$\mathcal F$: a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves
induces componentwise maps $C^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ commuting with the
differentials.

Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$,
and $\mathcal U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open cover indexed by a linearly ordered set,
with ordered Čech cochain complex $\bigl(C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F),
\delta^\bullet\bigr)$ ([[def-cech-cochain-complex-open-cover]],
[[lem-cech-differential-squares-zero]]). The **Čech cohomology of the fixed
cover $\mathcal U$ with values in $\mathcal F$** is
$$\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F) :=\ker\bigl(\delta^p:C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to C^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\bigr) \Big/\operatorname{im}\bigl(\delta^{p-1}:C^{p-1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\bigr),$$
the $p$-th cohomology group of the cochain complex
$\bigl(C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F),\delta^\bullet\bigr)$ in the sense of
[[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]. Since $C^{-1}(\mathcal U,
\mathcal F)=0$ and $\delta^{-1}=0$, one has $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)
=\ker(\delta^0)$, and for $p<0$ the group $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$
is $0$ because $C^p=0$, so both the kernel in degree $p$ and the image in degree $p$ are zero. A cochain in
$\ker(\delta^p)$ is called a **Čech $p$-cocycle** and a cochain in
$\operatorname{im}(\delta^{p-1})$ a **Čech $p$-coboundary**.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$. The topology
$\mathcal T_X$ is a set of open subsets. Fix a well-order of $\mathcal T_X$
using the Axiom of Choice, and let $\operatorname{Cov}(X)$ consist of all
subsets $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal T_X$ whose union is $X$, each indexed by
its distinct members in the inherited well-order. This is a set of ordered
covers. An arbitrary indexed open cover is represented by its distinct-member
cover: under Choice, one may choose an index for each distinct member, so the
two cover presentations refine one another and yield canonically isomorphic
Čech cohomology under refinement independence. For
$\mathcal U\in\operatorname{Cov}(X)$ write $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$
for its fixed-cover Čech cohomology
([[def-cech-cohomology-open-cover]]).

Say that $\mathcal U\preceq\mathcal V$, or that $\mathcal V$ **refines**
$\mathcal U$, when there is a refinement function from $\mathcal V$ to
$\mathcal U$, that is, a map $c$ from the index set of $\mathcal V$ to the index
set of $\mathcal U$ with $V\subseteq c(V)$ for every $V\in\mathcal V$
([[def-refinement-open-cover]]). This relation is a preorder: it is reflexive
through the identity map, and it is transitive because a composite of refinement
functions is a refinement function. It is **directed**: for covers
$\mathcal U,\mathcal V\in\operatorname{Cov}(X)$ the set of distinct intersections
$\mathcal W=\{U\cap V:U\in\mathcal U,\ V\in\mathcal V\}$ is another member of
$\operatorname{Cov}(X)$, indexed by the same inherited well-order, and covers
$X$. For each $W\in\mathcal W$, choose the least $U\in\mathcal U$ and the
least $V\in\mathcal V$ with $W=U\cap V$; the resulting maps refine
$\mathcal W$ to both covers. Repeating this construction stays within the same
set $\operatorname{Cov}(X)$.

The Axiom of Choice is used to fix transition data: for every pair
$\mathcal U\preceq\mathcal V$ choose one refinement function
$c_{\mathcal V\mathcal U}$ from $\mathcal V$ to $\mathcal U$. By
[[thm-refinement-map-independent-on-cohomology]] any two refinement functions
from $\mathcal V$ to $\mathcal U$ induce the same homomorphism
$\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check H^p(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$ in every
degree, so the chosen data give well-defined maps
$$\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\check H^p(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\qquad(\mathcal U\preceq\mathcal V),$$
and these maps are compatible with composition and with identities: the composite
of the chosen refinement functions along $\mathcal U\preceq\mathcal V\preceq\mathcal W$
is again a refinement function from $\mathcal W$ to $\mathcal U$ and hence
induces the composite of the two induced maps, while the identity is a refinement
function of a cover to itself and induces the identity. Thus
$\mathcal U\mapsto\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is a functor from the
directed preorder $\operatorname{Cov}(X)$ to the category of abelian groups.

The **Čech cohomology of $X$ with values in $\mathcal F$** is the filtered colimit
$$\check H^p(X,\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\mathcal U\in\operatorname{Cov}(X)}\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F),$$
taken in the category of abelian groups, of that functor ([[def-filtered-category-and-filtered-colimit]]). A class of
$\check H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ is represented by a pair $(\mathcal U,\alpha)$ with
$\mathcal U\in\operatorname{Cov}(X)$ and
$\alpha\in\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, and two such pairs represent the
same class exactly when the two classes agree after refinement to a common cover.
A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves induces the
maps $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ on fixed covers, which commute with the
refinement maps because the cochain maps of
[[def-refinement-open-cover]] are defined componentwise from the values of the
cochains; these maps pass to the filtered colimit and give
$$\check H^p(X,\varphi):\check H^p(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\check H^p(X,\mathcal G),$$
so that $\check H^p(X,-)$ is a functor on the abelian sheaves on $X$ with
$\check H^p(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for $p<0$.

Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of
$\mathbb R^m$ with its Euclidean metric. For every open cover $\mathcal U$ of
$\Omega$, there is a locally finite open cover $\mathcal V$ and a refinement
map $\rho:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ with $V\subseteq\rho(V)$ for every
$V\in\mathcal V$, such that each point of $\Omega$ lies in at most $m+1$
members of $\mathcal V$. Here locally finite means that every point has an
open neighborhood meeting only finitely many members, and the order bound
means the stated pointwise multiplicity bound.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its metric topology. Define
$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as the filtered colimit of the fixed-cover ordered
Čech cohomology groups over all open covers, and define $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as
the right derived functors of global sections from an injective resolution.
Then the canonical comparison
$$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
is a natural isomorphism for every integer $q\ge0$, compatible with the
identity identification of both degree-zero groups with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$.

derivations.claim: Let $\mathcal U$ be any open cover of $\Omega$. By [F4] it has a refinement $\mathcal V$ in which every point lies in at most $m+1$ members. For $q>m$, an increasing $(q+1)$-tuple has at least $m+2$ distinct members, so its intersection is empty; therefore every factor of $C^q(\mathcal V,\mathcal G)$ is the zero group by [F2], and $\check H^q(\mathcal V,\mathcal G)=0$.
Since every cover has such a refinement, the colimit over all covers in [F3] is zero in degree $q>m$: every representative becomes zero after refinement.
The comparison isomorphism [F5] identifies this zero colimit with $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal G)$, proving the ordinary sheaf cohomology bound. No compact-support comparison is invoked.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j$ and
$P'=\prod_{j=1}^n D'_j$ be finite open coordinate polydiscs such that each
closed coordinate disc $\overline{D'_j}$ is a compact subset of $D_j$. Let
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, and let $\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ be a
smooth form with $\bar\partial\eta=0$. Then there is a smooth
$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let
$\mathcal A=\mathcal C_M^\infty$ be its sheaf of real-valued smooth functions,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules. Then for every open
$U\subseteq M$ and every $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0.$$
The Axiom of Choice supplies injective resolutions for module sheaves and for
abelian-sheaf cohomology. Its consequences $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and DC supply,
respectively, the partitions of unity and the acyclic-resolution comparison
used below; no stronger choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

Assume the full axiom of choice. Let $n\ge1$ and let
$P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, where each $D_j$ is a nonempty
open disc of finite positive radius or is $\mathbb C$. For integers
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, every smooth
$\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ with $\bar\partial\eta=0$ is $\bar\partial$-exact:
there is a smooth $\omega\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P)$ such that
$\bar\partial\omega=\eta$. Consequently,
$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(P)=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $X$ be a topological space. Then
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ has enough injectives, every abelian sheaf on $X$ admits an
injective resolution ([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]), and
the embeddings below supply one injective resolution datum
([[def-supplied-injective-resolution-datum]]) on the whole category
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)$: for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ the datum assigns one
specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
built functorially from $\mathcal F$ with no further selection.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Let
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_{i+1}\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
be a sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space $X$. Then the
sequence is exact if and only if, for every point $x\in X$, the stalk sequence
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow (\mathcal F_{i-1})_x\xrightarrow{(d_{i-1})_x}(\mathcal F_i)_x\xrightarrow{(d_i)_x}(\mathcal F_{i+1})_x\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
is exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$$0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on a topological space $X$, and let
$H^q(X,-)$ be sheaf cohomology computed from the supplied functorial injective
resolution datum $I$ on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). Then there is a natural long
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^q(X,\mathcal F')\to H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X,\mathcal F'')\xrightarrow{\partial^q}H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F')\to H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
natural in the short exact sequence and independent of the choice of injective
resolutions used to assemble it.

The derived categories and right derived functor here are taken under the
standing smallness or supplied cofinal-denominator hypothesis of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a nonempty
open subset with its Euclidean metric, and let $\mathcal G$ be any sheaf of
abelian groups on $\Omega$. Then ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology
satisfies
$$H^q(\Omega,\mathcal G)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }q>m.$$
This is an ordinary cohomology bound for arbitrary sheaves; it is not a
compact-support cohomology assertion.

derivations.claim: If $N=0$, the chart neighborhood is the one-point space. Coherence makes the stalk a finitely generated $\mathbb C$-vector space, hence finite dimensional; choose a basis to identify $\mathcal F$ with a finite-rank free module on that point. Global sections on a point are the identity functor on abelian groups, so they are exact and have zero higher derived functors by [F7]. The Dolbeault complex consists only of degree-zero sections, and the isomorphism $\mathcal O^{p_0}\to\mathcal F$ preceded by the zero free module gives a partial free presentation with $\ell=1>2N=0$, exact at the required terms.

Suppose $N\ge1$. Apply [F2] with $\ell=2N+1$ and choose a coordinate polydisc $W$ about $x$ inside its chart neighborhood and $U$. Restrict the partial resolution to $W$. Write $K_0=\mathcal F|_W$ and, successively, let $K_{j+1}$ be the kernel of the induced surjection $\mathcal O_W^{p_j}\twoheadrightarrow K_j$ for $0\le j<\ell$. Exactness of the partial resolution gives these surjections; [F2] makes every $K_{j+1}$ coherent. Thus each sequence $$0\longrightarrow K_{j+1}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{p_j} \longrightarrow K_j\longrightarrow0$$ is short exact. The last kernel is the image of the leftmost map; no injectivity at that leftmost free term is needed.

Let $D\subseteq W$ be a nonempty coordinate polydisc. By [F3], the smooth Dolbeault sequence on $D$ is an exact resolution of $\mathcal O_D$. Its terms are modules over the sheaf of smooth functions, so [F4] makes them acyclic; [F5] therefore identifies $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)$ with the cohomology of the displayed global Dolbeault complex. By [F6] that global complex has zero cohomology in degrees $1\le q\le N$, and it is zero in degrees $q>N$. Hence $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for every $q>0$.

For each finite rank $p_j$, the restriction $\mathcal O_D^{p_j}$ is acyclic: step 1.3 gives acyclicity of each copy of $\mathcal O_D$, and [F7] gives additivity for the finite direct sum. Restricting the short exact sequences of step 1.2 to $D$ preserves exactness by [F8].

Fix $q>0$. In the long exact sequence of each restricted short exact sequence, the groups $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D^{p_j})$ and $H^{q+1}(D,\mathcal O_D^{p_j})$ vanish by step 2.1. Exactness from [F9] therefore makes the connecting homomorphism $$H^q(D,K_j|_D)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H^{q+1}(D,K_{j+1}|_D)$$ an isomorphism. Composing for $j=0,\ldots,\ell-1$ yields $$H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)\cong H^{q+\ell}(D,K_\ell|_D).$$

Since $D$ is open in $\mathbb R^{2N}$ and $q+\ell\ge1+(2N+1)>2N$, [F10] makes the right-hand group in step 3.1 zero. Hence $H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)=0$. The same $W$ works for every such $D$ and every $q>0$, because the partial resolution is fixed on $W$ and the scalar and dimension bounds apply to every open subpolydisc.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 retains the degree-zero Dolbeault term; vanishing is only asserted for q>0.
Steps 1.2 and 4.1 use ell=3>2 when N=1.
The N=0 point case and its length-one free presentation are handled separately in step 1.1.

boundaries.evidence: Full AC is explicit; for N≥1 the supplier is invoked with ell=2N+1 in step 1.2.

Fix $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and a polyradius $\rho$, let
$f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and separately holomorphic, let $r$
be a polyradius with $r_k<\rho_k$ for every $k<m$, and let

$$|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k},$$

and for every real $\theta$ with $0<\theta<1$ the series
$\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha$ converges absolutely and uniformly on
$\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$ with

$$f(z)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha\qquad(z\in\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)).$$

Since every $z\in\Delta_r(a)$ lies in $\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$ for some
$\theta<1$, the expansion holds throughout $\Delta_r(a)$.

**The coefficients are asserted here only as those iterated integrals.** That
$c_\alpha$ equals $\partial^\alpha f(a)/\alpha!$ needs termwise differentiation
and is not claimed by this statement.

Let $X$ be a topological space, let $x\in X$, and let $A$ be an abelian group.
The **skyscraper sheaf at $x$ with value $A$** is the sheaf
$$
i_{x,*}A
$$
defined on an open set $V \subseteq X$ by
$$(i_{x,*}A)(V)= \begin{cases} A,& x\in V,\\ 0,& x\notin V. \end{cases}$$
If $V' \subseteq V$ and both opens contain $x$, the restriction map is the
identity on $A$. If $x\notin V'$, the restriction map to $0$ is the unique zero
homomorphism.

Thus a skyscraper sheaf has the value $A$ precisely on opens that meet the
chosen point.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for
every $x\in X$, the induced map on stalks
$$\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\longrightarrow\mathcal G_x$$
is a bijection.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge0$, let $U$ be an open neighborhood
of $x\in\mathbb C^N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic
$\mathcal O_U$-module. A coordinate polydisc centered at $x$ means a set
$$W=\{z\in\mathbb C^N:|z_j-x_j|<r_j\ (1\le j\le N)\},\qquad r_j>0,$$
contained in $U$. There is such a $W$ for which the following hold.

For every nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subseteq W$ and every integer
$q>0$, ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology satisfies
$$H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)=0.$$
On each such $D$, scalar sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_D$ is computed by the
global smooth Dolbeault complex. Here $\mathcal A_D^{0,q}$ is the sheaf of
smooth complex-valued differential forms of type $(0,q)$ and $\bar\partial$ is
the Dolbeault differential:
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,0})\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots \xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,N}),$$
and in particular $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for $q>0$. The polydisc $W$ may be
chosen inside a neighborhood on which there is a partial finite-rank free resolution
$$\mathcal O_W^{p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal O_W^{p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map.

1. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on $X$, then $f_*\mathcal F$ is a sheaf on $Y$.
2. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of groups, rings, or modules on $X$, then
   $f_*\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of the same kind on $Y$.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for
every $x\in X$, the induced map on stalks
$$\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\longrightarrow\mathcal G_x$$
is a bijection.

Fix $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and a polyradius $\rho$, let
$f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be continuous and separately holomorphic, let $r$
be a polyradius with $r_k<\rho_k$ for every $k<m$, and let

$$c_\alpha:=\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{C_0}\!\cdots\!\int_{C_{m-1}} f(\zeta)\prod_{k<m}(\zeta_k-a_k)^{-\alpha_k-1}\,d\zeta_{m-1}\cdots d\zeta_0 ,$$

an iterated integral as in the polydisc Cauchy formula. Then, with

$\theta<1$, the expansion holds throughout $\Delta_r(a)$.

**The coefficients are asserted here only as those iterated integrals.** That
$c_\alpha$ equals $\partial^\alpha f(a)/\alpha!$ needs termwise differentiation
and is not claimed by this statement.

Let $m\ge1$, $a\in\mathbb C^m$ and let $r$ be a polyradius. Suppose
$c,c':\mathbb N^m\to\mathbb C$ both satisfy a bound
$|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k}$ and
$|c'_\alpha|\le M'\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k}$, and suppose

$$\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha=\sum_\alpha c'_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha \qquad\text{for every }z\in\Delta_r(a).$$

Then $c_\alpha=c'_\alpha$ for every multi-index $\alpha$. In particular a
function has at most one such power-series representation about a given centre,
and its coefficients are $\partial^\alpha_zf(a)/\alpha!$.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j$ and
$P'=\prod_{j=1}^n D'_j$ be finite open coordinate polydiscs such that each
closed coordinate disc $\overline{D'_j}$ is a compact subset of $D_j$. Let
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, and let $\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ be a
smooth form with $\bar\partial\eta=0$. Then there is a smooth
$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let
$\mathcal A=\mathcal C_M^\infty$ be its sheaf of real-valued smooth functions,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules. Then for every open
$U\subseteq M$ and every $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0.$$
The Axiom of Choice supplies injective resolutions for module sheaves and for
abelian-sheaf cohomology. Its consequences $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and DC supply,
respectively, the partitions of unity and the acyclic-resolution comparison
used below; no stronger choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

Assume the full axiom of choice. Let $n\ge1$ and let
$P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, where each $D_j$ is a nonempty
open disc of finite positive radius or is $\mathbb C$. For integers
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, every smooth
$\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ with $\bar\partial\eta=0$ is $\bar\partial$-exact:
there is a smooth $\omega\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P)$ such that
$\bar\partial\omega=\eta$. Consequently,
$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(P)=0$.

Let
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_{i+1}\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
be a sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space $X$. Then the
sequence is exact if and only if, for every point $x\in X$, the stalk sequence
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow (\mathcal F_{i-1})_x\xrightarrow{(d_{i-1})_x}(\mathcal F_i)_x\xrightarrow{(d_i)_x}(\mathcal F_{i+1})_x\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
is exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$$0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on a topological space $X$, and let
$H^q(X,-)$ be sheaf cohomology computed from the supplied functorial injective
resolution datum $I$ on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). Then there is a natural long
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^q(X,\mathcal F')\to H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X,\mathcal F'')\xrightarrow{\partial^q}H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F')\to H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
natural in the short exact sequence and independent of the choice of injective
resolutions used to assemble it.

The derived categories and right derived functor here are taken under the
standing smallness or supplied cofinal-denominator hypothesis of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

derivations.claim: On $D$, multiplication by $z_1$ gives a morphism $\mathcal O_D\to\mathcal O_D$. Restriction of holomorphic functions to $H_D$ is a morphism $\mathcal O_D\to i_*\mathcal O_{H_D}$ by [F3]–[F4], and it kills the image of multiplication by $z_1$. It therefore induces a morphism $\bar r:\mathcal Q\to i_*\mathcal O_{H_D}$. The quotient is coherent by [F1] and closure under cokernels in [F2].

At a point $a=(0,a')\in H_D$, a germ $h$ holomorphic on $H_D$ extends to $\widetilde h(z_1,z')=h(z')$, so $\bar r_a$ is surjective by [F3]. If $f$ is a holomorphic germ at $a$ whose restriction to $z_1=0$ vanishes, write its convergent expansion on a smaller product polydisc as $f(z_1,a'+\zeta')=\sum_{k,\alpha'}c_{k,\alpha'}z_1^k(\zeta')^{\alpha'}$. Since the restriction is the zero germ, [F6] implies $c_{0,\alpha'}=0$ for every $\alpha'$. The series $g(z_1,a'+\zeta')=\sum_{k\ge1,\alpha'}c_{k,\alpha'}z_1^{k-1}(\zeta')^{\alpha'}$ still converges on every smaller product polydisc, because shifting each positive $z_1$ exponent down by one preserves the positive radius of convergence. Thus $g$ is holomorphic and $f=z_1g$. The kernel of restriction on this stalk is exactly $(z_1)$, so $\bar r_a$ is an isomorphism.

On this arbitrary $D$, [F7] gives the exact smooth Dolbeault sheaf resolution of $\mathcal O_D$. Its terms are modules over smooth real-valued functions; [F8] makes them acyclic and identifies $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)$ with the cohomology of their global complex. By [F9] that complex has zero cohomology for $1\le q\le N$, and its terms are zero above degree $N$. Hence $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for every $q>0$.

If $a\in D\setminus H_D$, then $z_1(a)\ne0$, so the germ of $z_1$ is a unit and $\mathcal Q_a=0$. The stalk $(i_*\mathcal O_{H_D})_a$ is zero by [F3]. Together with step 1.2 this proves that $\bar r$ is an isomorphism on every stalk; [F5] gives the sheaf isomorphism.

Multiplication by $z_1$ is injective on every holomorphic stalk. Away from $H_D$ it multiplies by a unit. At $a=(0,a')\in H_D$, if $z_1f=0$ as a germ, expand $f$ on a sufficiently small product polydisc about $a$ using [F6]. Multiplication shifts every $z_1$ exponent up by one; uniqueness of the power-series coefficients therefore forces all coefficients of $f$ to vanish. Thus $f=0$. By [F10] multiplication is a sheaf monomorphism; its cokernel is $\mathcal Q$ by definition, giving the stated short exact sequence on the whole $D$.

Apply [F11] to the short exact sequence of step 2.2. For $q>0$, its segment $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)\to H^q(D,\mathcal Q)\to H^{q+1}(D,\mathcal O_D)$ has both outer groups zero by step 1.3, so $H^q(D,\mathcal Q)=0$. Its degree-zero segment also makes $\mathcal O(D)\to\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)$ surjective with kernel $z_1\mathcal O(D)$, because $H^1(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$. Finally the sheaf isomorphism of step 2.1 and the direct-image formula [F3] give $\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)=\Gamma(D,i_*\mathcal O_{H_D})=\mathcal O(H_D)$. Thus both the global quotient computation and all positive-degree vanishings hold for every coordinate polydisc containing $0$, using only scalar acyclicity and this multiplication sequence.

$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb C$ be of
class $C^1$ in the real coordinates
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], applied to the real
and imaginary parts of $f$ on $U$ read as an open subset of $\mathbb R^{2m}$).
Let $a\in U$. The following are equivalent.

1. $f$ is complex differentiable at $a$.
2. $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and its real total derivative
   $Df(a)$ is $\mathbb C$-linear.
3. $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and
   $\partial_{\bar z_k}f(a)=0$ for every $k<m$ — the several-variable
   Cauchy–Riemann system.

The $C^1$ hypothesis is used **only** to pass from the Cauchy–Riemann system to
real total differentiability; the implications from 1 to 2 and between 2 and 3
hold at any point with no regularity beyond what each condition states.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let
$\mathcal A=\mathcal C_M^\infty$ be its sheaf of real-valued smooth functions,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules. Then for every open
$U\subseteq M$ and every $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0.$$
The Axiom of Choice supplies injective resolutions for module sheaves and for
abelian-sheaf cohomology. Its consequences $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and DC supply,
respectively, the partitions of unity and the acyclic-resolution comparison
used below; no stronger choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^n$
be a domain, and suppose that $\Omega$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex
([[def-plurisubharmonic-exhaustion-and-hartogs-pseudoconvexity]]). Let
$1\le q\le n$.

1. **(Smooth vanishing.)** Every smooth $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,q)$-form
   $\eta\in\Omega^{0,q}(\Omega)$ ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]])
   is exact in the Dolbeault complex: there is
   $\zeta\in\Omega^{0,q-1}(\Omega)$ with $\bar\partial\zeta=\eta$.
   Consequently $H^{0,q}_{\bar\partial}(\Omega)=0$
   ([[def-dolbeault-cohomology-domain]]).

2. **(Weighted $L^2$ exactness under finite energy.)** Let
   $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ be strictly plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$
   ([[def-levi-form-and-strict-plurisubharmonicity]]); for $a\in\Omega$ let
   $\lambda_1(a)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(a)$ be the eigenvalues of the Hermitian
   matrix $(\varphi_{j\bar k}(a))$ and put
   $w(a):=\lambda_1(a)+\cdots+\lambda_q(a)>0$. If
   $f\in\operatorname{Dom}\bar\partial_q$ satisfies $\bar\partial_qf=0$ and
   $$E(f):=\int_\Omega|f|^2w^{-1}e^{-\varphi}\,dV<+\infty,$$
   then there is $u\in\operatorname{Dom}\bar\partial_{q-1}$ with
   $\bar\partial_{q-1}u=f$ and $\|u\|_\varphi^2\le E(f)$.

No boundary regularity of the primitives is claimed, and the statement is
asserted for $1\le q\le n$ only.

derivations.claim: On each coordinate polydisc in $\Omega$, [F2] says the sequence of sheaves $0\to\mathcal O_\Omega\to\mathcal A^{0,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{0,1}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots$ is exact in positive degree. Its degree-zero kernel is exactly $\mathcal O_\Omega$: a smooth function in that kernel has all $\bar z$-derivatives zero and is holomorphic by [F3]. Thus it is an exact sheaf resolution on $\Omega$.

Each resolution term is a sheaf of modules over smooth functions and is $\Gamma(\Omega,-)$-acyclic by [F4]. The acyclic-resolution theorem [F5] therefore identifies $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)$ with the cohomology in degree $q$ of the global smooth Dolbeault complex.

For $1\le q\le m$, [F6] makes every closed global smooth $(0,q)$-form exact, so the degree-$q$ cohomology in step 2.1 is zero. For $q>m$, the complex has no $(0,q)$-forms on an $m$-dimensional complex manifold, so its degree-$q$ cohomology is zero as well. Hence $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)=0$ for every $q>0$.

boundaries.reason: Omega is a Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain, hence a nonempty domain; the Statement is not an empty-open-set cohomology assertion.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: The asserted vanishings are only for q>0; degree zero is the holomorphic function space and need not vanish.
For m=1 the Dolbeault input supplies vanishing at q=1 and there are no (0,q) forms for q>1, exactly the split in proof 3.1.

boundaries.reason: Dimension m=0 is excluded by m>=1; the proof uses the positive-dimensional pseudoconvex-domain Dolbeault supplier.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 handles the top degree q=m by Dolbeault vanishing and every q>m by the absence of forms.
The Statement and step 2.1 use full AC for the acyclic-resolution and Dolbeault inputs.

boundaries.reason: Pseudoconvexity supplies global Dolbeault exactness, and the acyclic resolution transfers it to positive sheaf cohomology; no characterization of domains is claimed.
Vanishing of structure-sheaf cohomology is not used to reconstruct the Hartogs boundary-radius condition; the argument only consumes pseudoconvexity.

lem-qftx-gaga-scalar-pseudoconvex-acycli.finite_checks_disposition: The proof is a general Dolbeault-resolution argument; finite domains or degrees do not verify the universal analytic statement.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC) and the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a domain and let $u:\Omega\to\mathbb R$
be a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion, that is, $u$ is continuous and
plurisubharmonic and every sublevel set $\{z\in\Omega:u(z)\le c\}$,
$c\in\mathbb R$, is a compact subset of $\Omega$.

Then there exist a function $S\in C^\infty(\Omega)$ and a strictly increasing
sequence $c_1<c_2<\cdots$ with $c_k\to+\infty$ such that, writing
$\Omega_k:=\{z\in\Omega:S(z)<c_k\}$:

1. $S$ is strictly plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$, $S>u$ on $\Omega$, and $S$ is
   again an exhaustion of $\Omega$, that is, $\{z\in\Omega:S(z)\le c\}$ is a
   compact subset of $\Omega$ for every real $c$;
2. every $c_k$ is a regular value of $S$, and
   $\partial\Omega_k=\{z\in\Omega:S(z)=c_k\}$ is a nonempty $C^\infty$
   hypersurface of $\Omega$;
3. $\overline{\Omega_k}\subseteq\Omega_{k+1}$ and
   $\bigcup_{k\ge1}\Omega_k=\Omega$, so every $\overline{\Omega_k}$ is a compact
   subset of $\Omega$;
4. (strong pseudoconvexity) for every $k$, every $p\in\partial\Omega_k$ and
   every $v\in\mathbb C^n\setminus\{0\}$ with
   $$\sum_{j<n}\frac{\partial S}{\partial z_j}(p)\,v_j=0$$
   one has $\mathcal L_S(p;v)>0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a bounded domain with a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion $S$. Then $\Omega$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex: $-\log\delta_\Omega$ is plurisubharmonic, where $\delta_\Omega$ is the equal-radius polydisc boundary function.

Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be a Hartogs-pseudoconvex domain. Let $\mathcal O_\Omega$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. Then the derived sheaf cohomology satisfies $H^q(\Omega,\mathcal O_\Omega)=0$ for every integer $q>0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^n$
be a domain, and suppose that $\Omega$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex
([[def-plurisubharmonic-exhaustion-and-hartogs-pseudoconvexity]]). Let
$1\le q\le n$.

1. **(Smooth vanishing.)** Every smooth $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,q)$-form
   $\eta\in\Omega^{0,q}(\Omega)$ ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]])
   is exact in the Dolbeault complex: there is
   $\zeta\in\Omega^{0,q-1}(\Omega)$ with $\bar\partial\zeta=\eta$.
   Consequently $H^{0,q}_{\bar\partial}(\Omega)=0$
   ([[def-dolbeault-cohomology-domain]]).

2. **(Weighted $L^2$ exactness under finite energy.)** Let
   $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ be strictly plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$
   ([[def-levi-form-and-strict-plurisubharmonicity]]); for $a\in\Omega$ let
   $\lambda_1(a)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(a)$ be the eigenvalues of the Hermitian
   matrix $(\varphi_{j\bar k}(a))$ and put
   $w(a):=\lambda_1(a)+\cdots+\lambda_q(a)>0$. If
   $f\in\operatorname{Dom}\bar\partial_q$ satisfies $\bar\partial_qf=0$ and
   $$E(f):=\int_\Omega|f|^2w^{-1}e^{-\varphi}\,dV<+\infty,$$
   then there is $u\in\operatorname{Dom}\bar\partial_{q-1}$ with
   $\bar\partial_{q-1}u=f$ and $\|u\|_\varphi^2\le E(f)$.

No boundary regularity of the primitives is claimed, and the statement is
asserted for $1\le q\le n$ only.

Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a nonempty
open subset with its Euclidean metric, and let $\mathcal G$ be any sheaf of
abelian groups on $\Omega$. Then ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology
satisfies
$$H^q(\Omega,\mathcal G)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }q>m.$$
This is an ordinary cohomology bound for arbitrary sheaves; it is not a
compact-support cohomology assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$$0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on a topological space $X$, and let
$H^q(X,-)$ be sheaf cohomology computed from the supplied functorial injective
resolution datum $I$ on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). Then there is a natural long
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^q(X,\mathcal F')\to H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X,\mathcal F'')\xrightarrow{\partial^q}H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F')\to H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
natural in the short exact sequence and independent of the choice of injective
resolutions used to assemble it.

The derived categories and right derived functor here are taken under the
standing smallness or supplied cofinal-denominator hypothesis of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be a domain. A function
$u:\Omega\to[-\infty,\infty)$ is **plurisubharmonic** when:

1. $u$ is upper semicontinuous;
2. on no connected component of $\Omega$ is $u$ identically $-\infty$;
3. for every $a\in\Omega$ and every nonzero $v\in\mathbb C^m$, the function
   $$u_{a,v}(\lambda):=u(a+\lambda v)$$
   is subharmonic or identically $-\infty$ on each connected component of
   $$\{\lambda\in\mathbb C: a+\lambda v\in\Omega\}.$$

Fix an integer $m\ge1$. In this Definition, use one-based aliases for the canonical coordinates of
[[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]]: for $1\le j\le m$, the symbols
$z_j$ and $v_j$ denote the canonical coordinate and vector component with
index $j-1$. The derivatives $\partial_{z_j}$ and
$\partial_{\overline z_j}$ denote the corresponding canonical Wirtinger
operators of [[def-wirtinger-operators-in-several-complex-variables]] with
index $j-1$; all derivatives below use these aliases.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open and let $u\in C^2(\Omega,\mathbb R)$.
For $a\in\Omega$ and $v\in\mathbb C^m$, the **Levi form** of $u$ at $a$ in the
direction $v$ is

$$\mathcal L_u(a;v):=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{k=1}^m \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial z_j\partial\overline z_k}(a)\,v_j\overline{v_k}.$$

The function $u$ is **strictly plurisubharmonic** when

$$\mathcal L_u(a;v)>0\qquad\text{for every }a\in\Omega\text{ and every }v\ne0.$$

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open and let $u\in C^2(\Omega,\mathbb R)$.
Then $u$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$ if and only if

$$\mathcal L_u(a;v)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }a\in\Omega\text{ and every }v\in\mathbb C^m.$$

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be a domain.

1. If $u_1,\dots,u_N$ are plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$ and
   $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_N\ge0$, then
   $$\alpha_1u_1+\cdots+\alpha_Nu_N$$
   is plurisubharmonic, with the zero-coefficient terms omitted.
2. If $u_1,\dots,u_N$ are plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$, then
   $$u(z)=\max\{u_1(z),\dots,u_N(z)\}$$
   is plurisubharmonic.
3. If $u:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is plurisubharmonic and
   $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is convex and nondecreasing, then
   $\phi\circ u$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ and $V\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be domains, let
$F:\Omega\to V$ be holomorphic, and let $u\in C^2(V,\mathbb R)$ be
plurisubharmonic. Then $u\circ F$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$.

derivations.claim: Choose the chart of $D_{i_0}$ and write $V$ in those coordinates. For each $D_i$, the function $\rho_{D_i}$ in [F6] is a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion of $D_i$; on $V$ it remains plurisubharmonic after composing with the holomorphic chart transition. The continuous function $\rho:=\max_{1\le i\le s}\rho_{D_i}$ is plurisubharmonic by [F6]. If a sequence in $V$ leaves every compact subset of $V$, it approaches the boundary of at least one of the finitely many $D_i$, and the corresponding $\rho_{D_i}$ tends to $+\infty$. Thus $\rho$ is an exhaustion of $V$.

Each connected component $V_\alpha$ is a bounded domain in the chart of $D_{i_0}$ and inherits the continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion $\rho$. Apply [F1] to obtain a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion on $V_\alpha$, then [F2] to conclude that $V_\alpha$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex. By [F3], $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$, hence $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal O^{p})=0$ for every finite rank $p$.

Restrict the assumed partial resolution to $V_\alpha$ and define $K_{-1}=\mathcal F|_{V_\alpha}$ and $K_j=\ker(\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_j}\to\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_{j-1}})$ for $1\le j\le2r$, with $K_0=\ker(\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_0}\to K_{-1})$. Exactness of the resolution through the penultimate free term gives short exact sequences $0\to K_j\to\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}^{p_j}\to K_{j-1}\to0$ for $0\le j\le2r$, where at $j=0$ the rightmost term is $K_{-1}$. By [A1] each $K_j$ is coherent, and by step 2.1 the middle free sheaf in each sequence is acyclic in positive degree.

The long exact sequence [F5] for each short exact sequence in step 3.1 therefore gives, for every $q>0$, isomorphisms $H^q(V_\alpha,K_{j-1})\cong H^{q+1}(V_\alpha,K_j)$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,2r$. Iterating yields $H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal F)\cong H^{q+2r+1}(V_\alpha,K_{2r})$. The chart identifies $V_\alpha$ with an open subset of $\mathbb C^r\cong\mathbb R^{2r}$, so [F4] makes the last group zero because $q+2r+1>2r$.

The components of the open set $V$ are disjoint open subsets and are at most countable because the chart is second countable. Sheaves on their disjoint union are tuples of sheaves on the components; global sections are products, and products of abelian groups are exact under AC. Applying componentwise injective resolutions therefore gives $H^q(V,\mathcal F)=\prod_\alpha H^q(V_\alpha,\mathcal F)=0$ for $q>0$ by step 4.1.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement assumes V is nonempty; the empty intersection is excluded.
Statement: The conclusion is restricted to q>0; q=0 sections are not forced to be zero, and r=0 is excluded by r>=1.
Statement: For a single polydisc (s=1), its displayed exhaustion is already smooth strictly psh and the same length-2r resolution shifts positive cohomology above real dimension 2r.
Step 5.1 handles a disconnected V componentwise.
Statement: The shift is q+2r+1 after j=0,...,2r; for the first degree q=1 this is already strictly above 2r, so the cohomological-dimension bound is used strictly.
The Statement assumes full AC, used in step 5.1 for products over components.

boundaries.reason: The stated local Oka resolution and pseudoconvex intersection yield positive-degree acyclicity by proof 4.1; no converse resolution theorem is claimed.
Acyclicity of a given coherent sheaf does not here imply a finite-polydisc presentation or the local Oka assumptions; those remain supplied hypotheses.

lem-qftx-gaga-pseudoconvex-intersection-.finite_checks_disposition: The assertion concerns arbitrary finite polydisc intersections and coherent modules; finite examples cannot establish it.

citations.quote:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

For every integer $m\ge1$, the holomorphic germ ring $\mathcal O_{m,0}$ is a
Noetherian commutative ring.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, let $I\subset R$ be an ideal, let $M$
be a finite $R$-module, and let $N\subseteq M$ be a submodule. Then there exists
an integer $c\ge0$ such that
$$ I^nM\cap N = I^{n-c}(I^cM\cap N) $$
for every $n\ge c$.

The first clause below is choice-free; the second uses the published
Jacobson-radical unit criterion and therefore inherits its Axiom-of-Choice
boundary.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, let $I\subset R$ be an ideal, and let
$M$ be a finite $R$-module. Put
$$ K:=\bigcap_{n\ge0} I^nM. $$
Then:

1. $K$ is exactly the set of elements $m\in M$ for which $(1-a)m=0$ for some
   $a\in I$;
2. if $I\subseteq J(R)$, then $K=0$.

Let $m\ge1$, let $a\in\mathbb C^m$, let $\rho$ be a polyradius and let
$f:\Delta_\rho(a)\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic. Let $r$ be a polyradius with
$r_k<\rho_k$ for every $k<m$, and put $M=\sup_{\Gamma_r(a)}|f|$, the supremum
over the **distinguished boundary** only. Then for every multi-index $\alpha$

$$\bigl|\partial^\alpha_zf(a)\bigr|\ \le\ \alpha!\,M\prod_{k<m}r_k^{-\alpha_k}.$$

The bound uses no value of $f$ outside $\Gamma_r(a)$, which for $m\ge2$ is a
proper subset of the topological boundary of the closed polydisc.

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open, let each
$f_n:U\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic, and suppose $f_n\to f$ locally uniformly on
$U$: every point of $U$ has a neighbourhood on which the convergence is uniform.
Then $f$ is holomorphic on $U$, and for every multi-index $\alpha$

$$\partial^\alpha_zf_n\longrightarrow\partial^\alpha_zf$$

locally uniformly on $U$.

A **Fréchet space** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $E$ with a Hausdorff locally convex vector-space topology generated by a separating countable family of seminorms $(p_n)_{n\ge1}$ and complete for its seminorm uniformity. Explicitly, use the translation-invariant compatible metric
$$d(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\min\{1,p_n(x-y)\},$$
and require that this metric is complete. A seminorm is a function $p:E\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(cx)=|c|p(x)$ for $x,y\in E$ and $c\in\mathbb C$; separating means that for $x\ne0$ some $p_n(x)>0$. Locally convex means that every point has a neighborhood basis of convex sets. One may replace the defining family by the increasing family of its finite maxima.

Completeness here always refers to this vector-space uniformity. A sequence is Cauchy for the displayed metric exactly when it is Cauchy for every defining seminorm: each individual metric summand controls that seminorm at sufficiently small distances, and conversely the geometric tail of the metric series plus finitely many seminorm estimates controls the metric. Thus a seminorm-Cauchy series used in the accompanying proofs converges in $E$. The zero vector space is included, with its unique metric. This is the usual complete metrizable locally convex Fréchet convention.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge0$, let $U$ be an open neighborhood
of $x\in\mathbb C^N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic
$\mathcal O_U$-module. A coordinate polydisc centered at $x$ means a set
$$W=\{z\in\mathbb C^N:|z_j-x_j|<r_j\ (1\le j\le N)\},\qquad r_j>0,$$
contained in $U$. There is such a $W$ for which the following hold.

For every nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subseteq W$ and every integer
$q>0$, ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology satisfies
$$H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)=0.$$
On each such $D$, scalar sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_D$ is computed by the
global smooth Dolbeault complex. Here $\mathcal A_D^{0,q}$ is the sheaf of
smooth complex-valued differential forms of type $(0,q)$ and $\bar\partial$ is
the Dolbeault differential:
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,0})\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots \xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,N}),$$
and in particular $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for $q>0$. The polydisc $W$ may be
chosen inside a neighborhood on which there is a partial finite-rank free resolution
$$\mathcal O_W^{p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal O_W^{p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0$$
that is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except possibly the
leftmost one, with $\ell=2N+1>2N$. No exactness at the leftmost term and no
global free resolution are asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$$0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$$
be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on a topological space $X$, and let
$H^q(X,-)$ be sheaf cohomology computed from the supplied functorial injective
resolution datum $I$ on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). Then there is a natural long
exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H^q(X,\mathcal F')\to H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X,\mathcal F'')\xrightarrow{\partial^q}H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F')\to H^{q+1}(X,\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
natural in the short exact sequence and independent of the choice of injective
resolutions used to assemble it.

The derived categories and right derived functor here are taken under the
standing smallness or supplied cofinal-denominator hypothesis of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ and $F$ be Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$ and let $T:E\to F$ be a continuous, surjective, complex-linear map. Then $T$ is open: it sends every open subset of $E$ to an open subset of $F$.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaf. On an open set $V$ contained in a coordinate chart and in a neighborhood with a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$, where $p_0,p_1$ are finite nonnegative ranks, require that the section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Give $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ the compact-convergence topology generated by the seminorms $f\mapsto\sup_{z\in K}\lVert f(z)\rVert$ for compact $K\subset V$, and give $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology induced by that surjection. On any open subset covered by countably many such sets, use the topology of the closed subspace of the product of their local section spaces consisting of compatible families. For a finite ordered open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ whose nonempty finite intersections have these section topologies, give each Čech cochain space

$$C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_q},\mathcal F),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{q+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{q+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{q+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{q+1}}}.$$

the finite-product topology, give its cocycle space the subspace topology, and give the quotient of cocycles by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. The accompanying Fréchet-quotient lemma proves local chart and presentation independence; the compact projective-space finiteness theorem proves independence of its admissible finite acyclic cover topology.

derivations.claim: In chart coordinates, choose a compact exhaustion $K_1\subseteq K_2\subseteq\cdots$ of $V$, for example $K_n=\{z:|z|\le n,\ \operatorname{dist}(z,\mathbb C^m\setminus V)\ge1/n\}$, with distance to the empty set taken as $+\infty$. The seminorms $p_n(f)=\sup_{K_n}\|f\|$ generate compact-convergence. The resulting topology on $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ is Hausdorff and locally convex. A Cauchy sequence converges uniformly on each $K_n$ to a compatible continuous limit; it converges locally uniformly on $V$, so [F3] makes the limit holomorphic. Thus $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ is Fréchet.

Let $R=\mathcal O_{M,x}$ and let $L_x\subseteq R^{p_0}$ be the stalk of the relation sheaf $\ker(\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\to\mathcal F|_V)$. By [F1], $L_x$ is finitely generated. Artin–Rees in [F2] identifies the topology induced on $L_x$ from $R^{p_0}$ with its intrinsic Krull topology, while Krull intersection makes $R^{p_0}/L_x$ separated; thus $L_x$ is closed in the analytic Krull topology. If relation sections converge uniformly on compact subsets, [F3] makes every finite Taylor jet converge. For each $k$, the image of $L_x$ in the finite-dimensional jet space $R^{p_0}/\mathfrak m_x^kR^{p_0}$ is a linear subspace and hence closed. The limiting jet therefore lies in that image, so the limit germ belongs to $L_x+\mathfrak m_x^kR^{p_0}$ for every $k$. Krull intersection applied to the finite local module $R^{p_0}/L_x$ gives $\bigcap_k(L_x+\mathfrak m_x^kR^{p_0})=L_x$, proving the claimed membership explicitly. This holds at every $x$, and the sheaf-kernel condition puts the limit in the relation section space. Therefore the kernel of the global section map is closed in $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$.

A quotient of a Fréchet space by a closed linear subspace is Hausdorff and metrizable by the quotient seminorms. For completeness, choose a decreasing absolutely convex neighborhood basis $U_n$ in the original space such that $p_j(u)\le2^{-n}$ for $u\in U_n$ and $j\le n$, for a defining countable seminorm family $(p_j)$. From a Cauchy sequence of cosets choose a subsequence whose $n$th successive difference lies in the open quotient image of $U_n$, and lift that difference to some $u_n\in U_n$. For each fixed $j$, $\sum_n p_j(u_n)$ converges, so $(u_n)$ is summable in the Fréchet topology. Its sum gives a limit of the subsequence's cosets, and the original Cauchy sequence converges to the same coset. Local convexity descends through the open quotient map. Applying this argument to the closed kernel in step 1.2 proves the quotient topology is Fréchet.

Let two finite presentations be given near a point $x$, with coherent relation kernels $K,K'$ by [A2]. Apply [A3] to both kernels and intersect the resulting polydisc neighborhoods with the presentation neighborhoods. On a sufficiently small coordinate polydisc $D$ in this intersection, $H^1(D,K)=H^1(D,K')=0$. The long exact sequence [F5] for each presentation then proves that both section maps on $D$ are surjective. More generally, on any common open set $W$ where both presentations are defined and their section maps are surjective, lift the images of the finitely many basis sections of the first free module through the second section surjection. These lifts form a holomorphic matrix $A$ on $W$ with $\pi'A=\pi$. Multiplication by $A$ is continuous for compact-convergence because its entries are bounded on compact subsets; it induces the identity continuously between the quotient topologies. Reversing the presentations gives the reverse continuous identity. Thus the quotient topologies agree on each common presentation neighborhood. A holomorphic change of chart preserves compact-convergence because it and its inverse send compact subsets to compact subsets.

First consider a presentation neighborhood $V$ with its surjective section map and quotient topology. If a small chart polydisc $D\subseteq V$ has a target presentation whose section map is surjective, the restricted images of the finitely many source free generators lift to target free sections on $D$. As in step 3.1, these lifts give a holomorphic matrix on $D$. Restricting source free sections and multiplying by that matrix is continuous for compact-convergence, so passage through the two quotient maps proves continuity of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(D,\mathcal F)$. For any countable cover $(V_i)$ by such presentation neighborhoods, choose countably many sufficiently small polydiscs $D_{ij\nu}$ covering every overlap $V_i\cap V_j$, with surjective local section maps as in step 3.1. The restrictions from each $V_i,V_j$ into each such polydisc are continuous by the matrix argument. Therefore the compatible families are the intersection of the kernels of the continuous differences into $\Gamma(D_{ij\nu},\mathcal F)$. Those targets are Hausdorff Fréchet spaces by step 2.1, so this intersection is closed in the countable product of the local section spaces. A countable product of Fréchet spaces is Fréchet by enumerating their seminorms and taking componentwise limits; a closed subspace is complete for its restricted metric. Thus the compatible-family space is an actual Fréchet space. Compatibility checked on these overlap covers is full compatibility by the sheaf axiom.

To compare the quotient topology on an arbitrary presentation neighborhood $V$ with its topology from local sections, cover $V$ by countably many sufficiently small presentation polydiscs $(D_\nu)$ as in step 3.1. The restriction map from the already Fréchet quotient $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ into the compatible-family space for this cover is continuous by step 4.1. It is a linear bijection by unique sheaf gluing. Both its source and target are Fréchet by step 2.1 and step 4.1, so [F6] makes it a topological isomorphism. In particular, inverse gluing is continuous, and the original arbitrary-$V$ presentation quotient agrees with the compatible-family topology; no unproved identification of these topologies is made.

Any two countable presentation covers have a common countable refinement by sufficiently small presentation polydiscs; choose them inside the local vanishing neighborhoods of the finitely many relation kernels involved at each source-target comparison, as in step 3.1. Restriction from either compatible-family space into the refined compatible-family space is continuous by the local matrix argument of step 4.1 and is a bijection by sheaf gluing. All these spaces are Fréchet by step 4.1, so [F6] makes both maps topological isomorphisms. The identity on ordinary sections therefore identifies the two cover topologies. Together with the presentation and chart comparison in step 3.1 and the quotient-to-family comparison in step 5.1, this proves every asserted independence.
